definition_zh: 基岩；底岩；基础、根基；基本原则或核心信念
definition_en: the solid rock beneath loose soil and gravel, or the firm base on which something rests
core_image: 推土机铲掉表层土，露出灰白色的坚硬岩面，铲齿在上面打滑
scene: 推土机铲掉表层土后，司机下去敲了敲那层坚硬的灰岩，说下面再也挖不动了。 The drill stopped dead when it reached bedrock under the loose gravel.
sceneCN: 这里 bedrock 指「松散堆积物之下的坚硬基岩」（第 1 个义项：地表覆盖层之下的连续坚岩）；句意为钻头碰到砾石下面的基岩就再也钻不动了。图中可辨识物件：剥离的表土、灰白岩面、钻头、打滑的铲齿。

pos.zh: 基岩；底岩；（比喻）基础、根基、基本原则

senses.title: Solid rock under the soil
senses.titleCN: 松散覆盖层之下的连续坚岩
senses.definition: the continuous mass of solid rock that lies beneath soil, gravel and other loose material
senses.definitionCN: 位于土壤、砾石等松散物质之下的连续坚固体
senses.example: The well had to be drilled through nine metres of clay before it hit bedrock.
senses.exampleCN: 这口井穿过九米黏土才打到基岩。
senses.why: the compound is literal: the bed on which loose material rests, so hard that it is the reference surface for drilling.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是字面义：松散物质所躺的「床」，坚硬到成为钻探的参照面。

senses.title: The geological basement
senses.definition: the older, usually crystalline rock that underlies a sedimentary basin and its cover
senses.definitionCN: 位于沉积盆地及其盖层之下的较老、通常为结晶质的岩石
senses.example: The basin's bedrock is Archean gneiss, exposed only at the rim.
senses.exampleCN: 该盆地的基底是太古代片麻岩，只在边缘出露。
senses.why: geology uses the word for the floor of a basin, which may lie kilometres below the surface beds.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个词指盆地的底，它可能位于地表层之下数公里。

senses.title: The firm base of anything
senses.definition: the underlying support on which a structure, system or argument depends
senses.definitionCN: 结构、体系或论证所依赖的底层支撑
senses.example: Years of routine maintenance are the bedrock of a safe railway.
senses.exampleCN: 多年例行维护是安全铁路的基础。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the engineering sense: remove the base and everything above it settles or cracks.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留工程义：抽掉底座，上面的一切就会沉降或开裂。

senses.title: Core principles
senses.definition: the basic rules or values that a group treats as non-negotiable
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体视为不可让步的基本规则或价值
senses.example: Free inquiry is bedrock in any research university.
senses.exampleCN: 自由探究是任何研究型大学的根本原则。
senses.why: the word signals that these rules are not policies to be traded but the surface everything else is built on.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标示这些规则不是可交易的策略，而是其余一切所建的岩面。

senses.title: A reliable factual core
senses.definition: the verified facts that a case or claim can safely rest on
senses.definitionCN: 一项主张可以安全依托的、已被核实的事实
senses.example: The prosecution's case had bedrock: two witnesses and a signed ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 控方的案子有坚实基础：两名证人与一本签名的账簿。
senses.why: legal writing uses the image to separate what is proven from what is merely argued.
senses.whyCN: 法律写作借这个意象把已证之事与仅属论辩之事分开。

senses.title: A political stronghold
senses.definition: a region or group that reliably supports a party and is unlikely to swing
senses.definitionCN: 稳定支持某党、不易转向的地区或群体
senses.example: The northern valleys remain the party's bedrock.
senses.exampleCN: 北部各谷地仍是该党的票仓。
senses.why: politics borrows the word because such support is treated as terrain that cannot be moved.
senses.whyCN: 政治借用这个词，因为这种支持被视为搬不动的地形。

senses.title: The floor of a mine
senses.definition: the rock floor on which a seam or working rests, or the lowest level of a mine
senses.definitionCN: 煤层或工作面所坐的岩底，或矿井的最下层
senses.example: The seam was worked down to bedrock and then abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 煤层一直采到基岩底板，随后弃置。
senses.why: mining needs a precise word for the bottom, since everything above is measured from it.
senses.whyCN: 采矿需要一个精确的词指底，因为上面一切都以它为基准测量。

senses.title: The lowest social layer
senses.definition: the poorest or most excluded layer of a society, thought of as the floor beneath all others
senses.definitionCN: 社会中最贫困或最被排斥的一层，被视为其余各层之下的底
senses.example: Policy that ignores the bedrock of the housing market helps nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 忽视住房市场最底层的政策帮不到任何人。
senses.why: the image turns social stratification on its side: the lowest layer is also the one everything else presses down on.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象把社会分层横过来看：最下层也是其余一切向下压的那一层。

intro.en: Bedrock is an English compound of bed and rock, coined in the nineteenth century for the solid rock under loose deposits. Rock itself comes through Old Northern French from Medieval Latin rocca, a word of uncertain origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bedrock 是 bed 与 rock 的英语复合词，十九世纪为指松散沉积之下的坚岩而造。rock 经古北法语来自中世纪拉丁 rocca，该词来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bedd meant a sleeping place and, by extension, a flat layer on which something rests, as a river bed or a rock bed.
items.cn: bedd 指睡卧之处，引申为某物所躺的平面，如河床或岩层。

items.en: Rock entered Middle English from Old Northern French roque, which goes back to Medieval Latin rocca; the earlier history of that word is not settled.
items.cn: rock 经古北法语 roque 进入中古英语，上溯中世纪拉丁 rocca；该词更早的历史没有定论。

items.en: Geologists formed bedrock to name the solid mass below soil and alluvium, and the compound spread with drilling and mining.
items.cn: 地质学家造出 bedrock 以指土壤与冲积层之下的固体岩体，这个词随钻探与采矿传播开来。

items.en: Builders adopted it for the bearing surface a foundation must reach, which fixed the modern technical sense.
items.cn: 营造者采用它指基础必须达到的持力面，由此固定了现代技术义。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to the firm base of institutions, beliefs and arguments.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词被用于制度、信念与论证的坚实根基。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of rocca is unknown, and every form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：rocca 在拉丁语之前的谱系不明，凡为其提出的形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates bedrock from look-alikes that share one element but not the compound; group two separates it from words for bases and foundations.
note.cn: 第一组把 bedrock 与共享一个成分、却非同一复合词的形近词分开；第二组区分它与「基础」「根基」的近似说法。

entries.definition: By itself it means a sleeping place or a layer; bedrock adds the hardness and continuity of solid rock.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时指睡卧处或一层；bedrock 增添坚岩的硬度与连续性。

entries.definition: Any solid mineral matter, including loose boulders; bedrock specifically means the rock in place beneath cover.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指固体矿物，包括散落巨石；bedrock 特指覆盖层之下原地的岩体。

entries.definition: Bed plus sore, a skin injury from lying still; the shared first element is all they have in common.
entries.definitionCN: bed 加 sore，指久卧造成的皮肤损伤；共同点只在第一个成分。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for a foundation set directly on bedrock; it is a derived form, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指基础直接置于基岩上的技术形容词，是派生形式而非同义词。

entries.definition: The loose blanket of broken rock and soil above bedrock; the two words name the cover and the floor.
entries.definitionCN: 基岩之上破碎岩石与土壤的松散覆盖层；两词一名盖、一名底。

entries.definition: The constructed base of a building, which may or may not reach bedrock; it is man-made, bedrock is not.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的人造底座，未必达到基岩；foundation 是人造的，bedrock 不是。

entries.definition: A ceremonial stone or a figurative essential part; it stresses origin and symbolism, not geological depth.
entries.definitionCN: 奠基仪式用的石块，或比喻最要紧的部分；强调起源与象征，而非地质深度。

entries.definition: The broadest word for what something stands on, physical or abstract, without the hardness of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物所立之处的最宽泛词，实体或抽象皆可，不含岩石的坚硬。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bed 'resting surface' + rock: the rock that everything else lies on.
normal.cn: bed「所躺之面」+ rock：其余一切所躺的那块岩。

normal.en: Drillers treat bedrock as the reference surface, which is why 'reach bedrock' also means 'reach the bottom of the matter'.
normal.cn: 钻探者把基岩当作参照面，因此「钻到基岩」也引申为「触及根本」。

normal.en: The word pairs naturally with overburden and regolith, its loose cover.
normal.cn: 这个词天然与 overburden 和 regolith（松散覆盖层）配对。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: bedrock geology, bedrock principle, bedrock belief.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：基岩地质、根本原则、核心信念。

normal.en: The metaphor keeps the engineering sense: no base, no building.
normal.cn: 这个比喻保留工程义：没有底座，就没有建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a drill bit screaming to a stop on grey stone.
abstract.cn: 想象钻头在灰岩上尖叫着停住。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose lowest course of stone sits directly on clean rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋房，最下一层石料直接坐在净岩上。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that collapses the moment one plain fact is removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个论证，抽掉一条朴素事实就整个垮掉。

examples.en: The bridge piers are founded on bedrock, not on the river gravel.
examples.cn: 桥墩立在基岩上，而非河砾之上。

examples.en: Trust between doctors and patients is the bedrock of the clinic.
examples.cn: 医患之间的信任是这家诊所的根基。

examples.en: Weathering has eaten the bedrock into a rough pavement.
examples.cn: 风化把基岩啃成一片粗糙的石面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bed（床）+ rock（岩）」——岩做的床，压在最下面 → 基岩、根基

root: 英语 bed（古英语 bedd「躺卧之处、底」）+ rock（经古北法语 roque，上溯中世纪拉丁 rocca，来源不确定）；十九世纪地质复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one image, the rock at the bottom: first the geological floor, then any firm base, then the rules, facts, voters and people that everything else presses down on.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都依托同一个意象——最下面那块岩：先是地质底，再是任何坚实基础，然后是规则、事实、票源以及其余一切向下压的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard grey floor under everything loose, unmistakable when the drill reaches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：松散之物下面一层坚硬的灰岩面，钻头碰到时不会认错。

branches.en: GEOLOGICAL FLOOR: the surface under cover and the basement under a basin are the same rock seen at two scales.
branches.cn: 地质底：覆盖层之下的面与盆地之下的基底，是同一块岩的两种尺度。

branches.en: FIRM SUPPORT: a structure and a case both fail if the base is removed.
branches.cn: 坚实支撑：结构与案子一旦抽掉底座都会垮。

branches.en: CORE RULES: principles are treated as terrain, not as tradable policy.
branches.cn: 核心规则：原则被当作地形，而非可交易的策略。

branches.en: TERRAIN AND FLOOR: safe seats and mine floors are both places nothing above can move.
branches.cn: 地形与底板：稳固票仓与矿井底板都是上面之物搬不动的地方。

branches.en: SOCIAL BOTTOM: the lowest layer bears the weight of all the others.
branches.cn: 社会底层：最下一层承着其余各层的重量。

intro.en: Bedrock is a native English compound, so its parts are read as ordinary nouns rather than as Latin morphemes.
intro.cn: bedrock 是本族英语复合词，其成分应按普通名词而非拉丁语素来读。

latinIntro.en: Bed is native Old English; rock reaches English through French and Medieval Latin rocca, whose own origin is uncertain, so no confident Latin root is offered.
latinIntro.cn: bed 为本族古英语词；rock 经法语与中世纪拉丁 rocca 进入英语，而 rocca 自身来源不确定，因此不给出有把握的拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 诱骗；迷惑；使着迷（消磨时光）
definition_en: to charm or trick someone, often deceptively; also to pleasantly occupy time
core_image: 蛇用甜言把人引向岔路
scene: 集市上，兜售假货的商贩巧舌如簧。 The pedlar beguiled the villagers into buying his worthless charms.
sceneCN: 这里 beguiled 是「诱骗」（第 1 个义项：以魅力或花言巧语欺骗）；句意是商贩花言巧语哄村民买下毫无价值的护身符。

pos.zh: 诱骗；迷惑；消磨（时光）

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转形容词，义为「迷人的；诱人的」
由 beguile 加 -ment 构成，义为「迷惑；消遣」

senses.title: To trick by charm
senses.definition: to deceive someone, often using charm or flattery
senses.definitionCN: 欺骗某人，常借助魅力或谄媚
senses.example: The pedlar beguiled the villagers into buying his worthless charms.
senses.exampleCN: 商贩花言巧语哄村民买下毫无价值的护身符。
senses.why: The base word guile means deceit, so beguile is deceit set in motion.
senses.whyCN: 词基 guile 意为「欺诈」，beguile 即「把欺诈付诸行动」。

senses.title: To charm pleasantly
senses.definition: to delight or enchant someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某人愉悦或着迷
senses.example: Her storytelling beguiled the children for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲故事让孩子们着迷了好几个钟头。
senses.why: Charm can be innocent, so the word softened to mean simply enchanting.
senses.whyCN: 魅力未必存恶意，故词义软化，单指「令人着迷」。

senses.title: To while away time
senses.definition: to occupy time pleasantly
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地打发时间
senses.example: They beguiled the long train ride with cards and gossip.
senses.exampleCN: 他们靠打牌闲谈打发漫长的火车旅程。
senses.why: Enchantment makes hours pass unnoticed.
senses.whyCN: 沉醉使时光不知不觉流逝。

intro.en: Beguile adds be- to guile, deceit.
intro.cn: beguile 在 guile（欺诈）前加 be-。

items.en: guile came through Old French guile, trickery.
items.cn: guile 经古法语 guile「诡计」传入。

items.en: the French word is generally traced to Frankish wigala, a snare or ruse; the trail is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语词一般追溯到法兰克语 wigala「圈套、诡计」，线索存疑。

items.en: beguile appeared as a verb of deceiving.
items.cn: 中古英语 beguile 作「欺骗」义的动词出现。

items.en: the sense of charming and amusing grew alongside deceit.
items.cn: 十六世纪「迷住、娱悦」义与「欺骗」义并行发展。

items.en: beguiling now usually suggests enchantment more than fraud.
items.cn: 如今 beguiling 更多表示「迷人」而非「行骗」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or the guile root; the near-meaning group gathers charming and deceiving words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或 guile 词根；近义组汇集迷人与欺骗类词。

电离；发生电离

由 ionize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已电离的」
由 ionize 加进行词尾构成，义为「致电离的」
由 ionize 加施动词尾构成，义为「离子发生器」

senses.title: Strip electrons from neutral matter
senses.titleCN: 从中性物质中剥出电子
senses.definition: to make neutral atoms or molecules become ions by removing or adding electrons
senses.definitionCN: 通过移走或加上电子，使中性原子或分子变成离子
senses.example: A high-voltage field can ionize the surface molecules so that ink grips.
senses.exampleCN: 高压电场能使表面分子电离，好让油墨附着。
senses.why: The verb carries the plain causative reading: an outside agent acts on matter, and the result is ions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词携带直白的致使义：外部作用者施力于物质，结果就是离子。

senses.title: Become ionic without an agent
senses.definition: to undergo ionization naturally, as a gas or liquid does when conditions allow
senses.definitionCN: 在条件允许时像气体或液体那样自然发生电离
senses.example: At very high temperatures the vapour begins to ionize on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 在极高温度下，蒸气开始自行电离。
senses.why: The same event is viewed without an agent, so the verb shifts to the intransitive pattern: the substance simply undergoes the change.
senses.whyCN: 同一事件在不提作用者时被观察，于是动词转为不及物：物质自身经历这一变化。

senses.title: Make a gas conduct
senses.definition: to create free charges in a gas so that it can carry a current
senses.definitionCN: 在气体中产生自由电荷，使其能够承载电流
senses.example: A spark first ionizes the air, and then the arc can jump.
senses.exampleCN: 火花先使空气电离，电弧随后才能跳过。
senses.why: Ionizing a gas is usually done to change what the gas can do; the purpose is conductivity, not the ions themselves.
senses.whyCN: 使气体电离通常是为了改变气体的能力；要点是导电，而不是离子本身。

senses.title: Split water or acid molecules
senses.definition: to cause water or an acid to separate into charged parts in solution
senses.definitionCN: 使水或酸在溶液中分离成带电部分
senses.example: Water ionizes only slightly unless an acid is present.
senses.exampleCN: 除非有酸存在，水只会轻微电离。
senses.why: The object here is a molecule that splits rather than a gas that is struck, and the verb still means the coming-into-being of ions.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对象是发生分裂的分子，而不是被撞击的气体，动词仍指离子的产生。

senses.title: Ionize by radiation
senses.definition: to knock electrons out of matter with high-energy particles or rays
senses.definitionCN: 用高能粒子或射线把电子从物质中打出
senses.example: Cosmic rays ionize the upper atmosphere every day.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线每天都在使高层大气电离。
senses.why: Radiation is the classic natural agent of the change, so the verb routinely takes radiation as the unstated doer.
senses.whyCN: 辐射是这一变化最典型的天然作用者，因此动词常以辐射为不言自明的主角。

senses.title: Ionize a sample inside an instrument
senses.definition: to charge sample molecules in a mass spectrometer so their fragments can be measured
senses.definitionCN: 在质谱仪中使样品分子带电，以便测量其碎片
senses.example: The instrument ionizes the sample before the fragments are weighed.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器先使样品电离，然后称量碎片。
senses.why: Instrument ionizing is deliberate and repeated, turning the verb into a step in a procedure rather than a natural event.
senses.whyCN: 仪器中的电离是有意反复执行的，于是动词变成流程里的一个步骤，而非自然事件。

senses.title: Ionize atoms in a hot flame
senses.titleCN: 在高温火焰中使原子电离
senses.definition: to charge atoms thermally in a flame or arc for spectroscopy
senses.definitionCN: 在火焰或电弧中借高温使原子带电，用于光谱分析
senses.example: The flame ionizes a fraction of the atoms before they emit light.
senses.exampleCN: 火焰在原子发光前先使其中一部分电离。
senses.why: Heat is another agent of the same change, and the verb keeps its plain sense while the setting becomes an analytical burner.
senses.whyCN: 热是同一变化的另一种作用者；环境换成分析用燃烧器，动词的含义仍旧朴素。

senses.title: Ionize a surface for treatment
senses.titleCN: 为表面处理而使之电离
senses.definition: to charge the molecules on a surface so that coatings, inks or films adhere properly
senses.definitionCN: 使表面分子带电，好让涂层、油墨或薄膜正常附着
senses.example: Factories ionize plastic film so that printed layers do not peel off.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂使塑料薄膜电离，好让印上去的层不脱落。
senses.why: The industrial use applies the event to a flat object, and the aim is adhesion rather than conductivity or measurement.
senses.whyCN: 工业用法把这一事件用在平面上，目的既不是导电也不是测量，而是附着。

intro.en: Ionize is a nineteenth-century English verb built on ion, itself coined in 1834 from a Greek participle meaning 'going'. Its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: ionize 是 19 世纪在 ion 基础上构成的英语动词，而 ion 本身是 1834 年据一个意为「行走的」希腊语分词所造；其首见年代为约数。

items.en: The Greek verb ienai 'to go' supplied the participle ion, literally 'that which goes', which Faraday used for the charged particles drifting to the poles.
items.cn: 希腊语动词 ienai「走」提供了分词 ion，字面是「行走之物」，法拉第用它指漂向两极的带电粒子。

items.en: Once ion had become the ordinary English noun for a charged particle, speakers had a base for a verb of making such particles.
items.cn: ion 一旦成为指带电粒子的普通英语名词，人们就有了造出「制造此类粒子」动词的基础。

items.en: The ending -ize reached English through French and ultimately Greek, and it turns a noun into the action of producing or becoming that noun.
items.cn: 动词词尾经法语上溯至希腊语进入英语，其作用是把名词变成「产出该物或变成该物」的动作。

items.en: The verb appeared in the middle of the nineteenth century as the study of electrolysis and electrical discharge expanded; the earliest citation is not securely fixed.
items.cn: 这个动词出现在 19 世纪中叶，正值电解与放电研究扩展之时；最早的引文年代并未确凿固定。

items.en: Mass spectrometry, radiation medicine and plasma physics made the verb a routine technical step, and compound uses such as ionizing radiation followed.
items.cn: 质谱、放射医学与等离子体物理使它成为常规技术步骤，致电离辐射一类的复合用法随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain for the deeper root: the pre-Greek origin of ienai is not established, and any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 更深词根来源不确定：ienai 在希腊语之前的来源尚未确立，为它引用的更古老形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group shares the ion stem but differs in what kind of word each is; the second group describes other ways of breaking matter into charged parts.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ion 词干，但各词所属的词类不同；第二组描述把物质拆成带电部分的其他方式。

entries.definition: The charged particle that results; it cannot take an object and names no action.
entries.definitionCN: 由此产生的带电粒子；它不能带宾语，也不命名动作。

entries.definition: The event of producing ions; the verb ionize is what one does to bring it about.
entries.definitionCN: 产生离子的事件；而 ionize 是促成它时所做的动作。

entries.definition: An adjective or participle describing matter that has already acquired charge, not the act of charging it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或分词，描述已经带上电荷的物质，而不是使其带电的动作。

entries.definition: A machine that performs the ionizing; it names the doer, while the verb names the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 执行电离的机器；它命名施动者，而动词命名动作。

entries.definition: To break a molecule into smaller parts, often charged ones; the emphasis is on the severed bond, not on the resulting charge.
entries.definitionCN: 把分子拆成更小、常带电的部分；重点在断开的键，不在产生的电荷。

entries.definition: To supply electric charge to an object; it can be done without changing the object into ions.
entries.definitionCN: 给物体提供电荷；这样做并不必然把物体变成离子。

entries.definition: To decompose a substance by passing a current through it; ionization supplies the carriers, but current does the forcing.
entries.definitionCN: 通电流使物质分解；电离提供载流子，但施力的是电流。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ion plus the verb ending -ize: to make ions.
normal.cn: ion 加动词词尾：使成为离子。

normal.en: The family runs ion, ionize, ionized, ionizing, ionizer, ionization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ion、ionize、ionized、ionizing、ionizer、ionization。

normal.en: Typical objects in fixed phrases: ionize a gas, ionize the air, ionize molecules.
normal.cn: 固定搭配里的典型宾语：使气体电离、使空气电离、使分子电离。

normal.en: Radiation is the natural doer: cosmic rays ionize the upper air.
normal.cn: 辐射是天然作用者：宇宙射线使高层大气电离。

normal.en: Industry ionizes surfaces so that ink and coatings stick.
normal.cn: 工业上使表面电离，好让油墨与涂层附着。

abstract.en: Picture a comb rubbed until it pulls scraps of paper toward itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梳子被摩擦到能把纸屑吸向自己。

abstract.en: Picture a lock that opens only after one small part is flicked out of place.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁，只有把一个小零件弹离原位才打得开。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond touched at one point until ripples carry outward in rings.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭静水在一点被触动，涟漪一圈圈向外传开。

examples.en: Gamma rays ionize the molecules they pass through.
examples.cn: 伽马射线会使其穿过的分子电离。

examples.en: The technician ionized the sample with a beam of electrons.
examples.cn: 技术员用电子束使样品电离。

examples.en: Certain plastics are ionized before they are printed.
examples.cn: 某些塑料在印刷前要经过电离处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ion（离子）+ ize（使）」——使东西变成离子

root: 英语 ion（1834 年据希腊语 ienai「行走」的中性分词所造）+ 动词词尾；更早词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of stripping charge: the plain act with an agent, the act without one, the gas made conductive, water and acids split, radiation as doer, the instrument step, the hot flame, and the industrial surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个剥离电荷的动作：有作用者的直白动作、无作用者的自变、气体变得导电、水与酸离解、以辐射为作用者、仪器步骤、高温火焰与工业表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a charged field pulls electrons off a surface, and loose charged specks settle where they are wanted.
core.cn: 核心意象：带电电场把电子从表面扯下，散开的带电微粒落在需要它们的地方。

branches.en: THE ACT WITH OR WITHOUT A DOER: something strips the charge, or the substance does it on its own.
branches.cn: 有作用者与无作用者的动作：要么外物剥去电荷，要么物质自己完成。

branches.en: WHY IT IS DONE: free charges are created so that a gas can at last carry a current.
branches.cn: 为何要做：造出自由电荷，好让气体终于能承载电流。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE INSTEAD: water and acids split into charged parts inside a solution.
branches.cn: 换成分子：水与酸在溶液里分裂成带电部分。

branches.en: THE AGENTS: rays and heat do the stripping, one natural and one industrial.
branches.cn: 作用者：射线与高温完成剥离，一个天然，一个工业。

branches.en: THE SETTINGS: a mass spectrometer charges a sample, and a factory charges a film so that ink holds.
branches.cn: 场景：质谱仪使样品带电，工厂使薄膜带电好让油墨附着。

intro.en: Ionize is one root plus one ending, and the same ending recurs across thousands of English verbs.
intro.cn: ionize 由一个词根加一个词尾构成，而这个词尾出现在成千上万个英语动词里。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek; Latin only supplies the verb ending that reached English through French, so no Latin cognate of the root is given.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语；拉丁语只提供了经法语进入英语的动词词尾，因此不列出词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The noun ion names the product of the act.
items.exampleCN: 名词 ion 命名这一动作的产物。

items.structure: verb-forming ending, through French from Greek
items.example: The ending turns a noun into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成「制造」类动词。

items.meaning: the process of making or becoming
items.example: The noun ending turns the act into a process.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾把动作变成过程。

items.example: The ionized film holds the ink.
items.exampleCN: 经过电离的薄膜能挂住油墨。
离子发生器使空气带电。

items.structure: ionize plus the action noun ending
items.meaningCN: 使物质成为离子的过程
items.example: Ionization raises the conductivity of the gas.
items.exampleCN: 电离提高了气体的导电性。

definition_zh: 分解；腐烂；使腐败
definition_en: to break something down into simpler parts or substances
core_image: 一块木头在湿土里一年年变软、变空、最后消失
scene: 雨后的林地里，倒木正在慢慢瓦解： Fungi decompose the fallen trunk until only a dark line of soil remains.
sceneCN: 这里 decompose 是「分解、腐烂」（第 2 个义项：有机物被真菌分解）；句意：真菌分解这根倒下的树干，最后只剩一道深色的土痕。

pos.zh: 使分解；使腐烂；拆解（使某物分解）
分解；腐烂；崩解（自行分解）

senses.title: Split a compound chemically
senses.definition: to separate a compound into simpler substances by chemical action
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学作用把化合物分离成更简单的物质
senses.example: Strong heat decomposes the carbonate into oxide and gas.
senses.exampleCN: 高温把这种碳酸盐分解为氧化物和气体。
senses.why: The verb undoes a combination: de- takes apart what compose had put together.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把「组合」拆掉：de- 把 compose 曾经放在一起的东西分开。

senses.title: Rot away
senses.definition: of dead organic matter, to decay into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 指死亡的有机物腐烂成更简单的物质
senses.example: The leaves decompose faster when the soil stays moist.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤保持湿润时，落叶分解得更快。
senses.why: Decay is chemical decomposition happening without a flask, carried out by microbes and water.
senses.whyCN: 腐败就是没有烧瓶的化学分解，由微生物与水来完成。

senses.title: Make something rot
senses.definition: to cause organic material to decay, used with a subject that acts on the object
senses.definitionCN: 使有机材料腐烂，主语对宾语施加作用
senses.example: Bacteria decompose the manure before the field is planted.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在整地之前把粪肥分解掉。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an agent: someone or something sets the breakdown going.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加了施动者：某人或某物让分解开始发生。

senses.title: Split a mathematical object
senses.definition: to express a function, matrix or number as a product or sum of simpler parts
senses.definitionCN: 把函数、矩阵或数表示成更简单部分的乘积或和
senses.example: The program decomposes the matrix before solving the system.
senses.exampleCN: 程序在求解方程组之前先把矩阵分解。
senses.why: Mathematics reuses the verb because the operation is a structured taking-apart, not physical decay.
senses.whyCN: 数学复用这个动词，因为该操作是结构化的拆分，而不是物理腐败。

senses.title: Divide a problem into parts
senses.definition: in computing, to divide a task or system into smaller parts that can be handled separately
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把任务或系统划分成可分别处理的更小部分
senses.example: We decompose the pipeline into stages that can run in parallel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这条流水线拆成可以并行运行的若干阶段。
senses.why: Software work repeats the same gesture at the level of tasks, where the parts are functions rather than molecules.
senses.whyCN: 软件工作在任务层面重复同一动作，只是拆出的部分成了功能而不是分子。

senses.title: Take an argument apart
senses.definition: to analyse a text or argument by separating its claims and assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 通过分离主张与假设来分析文本或论证
senses.example: The class decomposed the editorial into three unsupported claims.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂上把这篇社论拆解成三个缺乏支持的断言。
senses.why: Analytical reading is decomposition in the mind, where the pieces are claims rather than compounds.
senses.whyCN: 分析性阅读是心智中的分解，拆出的碎片是论点而不是化合物。

senses.title: Break down after death
senses.definition: of a body, to pass through the stages of post-mortem breakdown
senses.definitionCN: 指尸体经历死后的各个崩解阶段
senses.example: The body had decomposed for weeks before it was found.
senses.exampleCN: 尸体被发现时已经分解了数周。
senses.why: Forensic writing uses the verb for the whole sequence, keeping the tone clinical rather than emotional.
senses.whyCN: 法医写作使用这个动词描述整个序列，语气保持临床化而非情绪化。

senses.title: Fall apart figuratively
senses.definition: of an organisation, plan or relationship, to disintegrate gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指组织、计划或关系逐渐瓦解
senses.example: The coalition decomposed into rival factions within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联盟在一年之内瓦解成相互对立的派系。
senses.why: The image of a structure losing its bonds transfers easily to institutions that lose their internal ties.
senses.whyCN: 「结构失去结合」的形象很容易移用到失去内部纽带的机构上。

intro.en: Decompose was formed in French chemistry and then borrowed into English; its Latin parts are de- and componere.
intro.cn: decompose 在法国化学中形成，随后借入英语；其拉丁语成分是 de- 与 componere。

items.en: Compose comes from Latin componere 'to put together', from com- 'together' and ponere 'to place'. The same ponere underlies position, deposit, impose and postpone.
items.cn: compose 来自拉丁语 componere「放在一起」，由 com-「共同」与 ponere「放置」构成。同一个 ponere 也是 position、deposit、impose、postpone 的词根。

items.en: In de- the prefix carries the sense 'apart, away, down', so the new verb means to undo a putting-together.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 带有「分开、离开、向下」之意，因此新动词表示「撤销一次组合」。

items.en: French décomposer is recorded in eighteenth-century chemical writing, when analysts were learning to split compounds into elements. English adopted the verb soon after.
items.cn: 法语 décomposer 见于 18 世纪的化学写作，当时分析家正学着把化合物拆成元素。英语很快借入了这个动词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology applied decompose to rotting organisms, giving the everyday sense its scientific footing.
items.cn: 19 世纪的生物学把 decompose 用于腐烂的生物体，使这个日常义项获得科学依据。

items.en: Mathematics and computing later borrowed the verb for structured splitting, while figurative use for failing institutions followed naturally. The first recorded date of each extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 数学与计算随后借用这个动词表示结构化拆分，用于失败机构的比喻用法也自然跟进。各个延伸义项的确切首见年代尚无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the root; the second holds other verbs of breaking down.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根；第二组是其他表示「崩解」的动词。

entries.definition: The process or result; decompose is the action that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或结果；decompose 是产生这一过程的动作。

entries.definition: To put together or create; decompose reverses exactly that direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西组合起来或创作；decompose 正是把这一方向反过来。

entries.definition: The organism or device doing the work; it cannot replace the verb in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；不能用来替代句中的动词。

entries.definition: To decay naturally, often with a smell; decompose is the neutral term used in science.
entries.definitionCN: 自然腐烂，常带气味；decompose 是科学中的中性说法。

entries.definition: A general phrasal verb for failure or separation, applied to machines and emotions as well as matter.
entries.definitionCN: 通用短语动词，表示故障或分离，可用于机器、情绪与物质。

entries.definition: To break into fragments, often violently or completely; decompose stresses chemical change rather than mechanical shattering.
entries.definitionCN: 碎成小块，常含剧烈或彻底之意；decompose 强调化学变化而非机械碎裂。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the reversal prefix and the verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表反转的前缀与动词形式。

normal.en: compose = put together; decompose = take apart.
normal.cn: compose 是放在一起，decompose 是拆开。

normal.en: The forms follow the regular pattern: decomposes, decomposed, decomposing.
normal.cn: 词形变化规律：decomposes、decomposed、decomposing。

normal.en: The object tells you the sense: decompose a compound, a leaf, a matrix, a problem.
normal.cn: 看宾语就能判断义项：分解化合物、落叶、矩阵或问题。

normal.en: The root ponere 'place' links it to position, deposit and impose.
normal.cn: 词根 ponere「放置」把它与 position、deposit、impose 联系起来。

normal.en: The soil under a fallen log is the word's home ground.
normal.cn: 倒木下面的土壤，就是这个词的主场。

abstract.en: Think of a knot loosening thread by thread until the rope is only fibre.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结一根线一根线地松开，直到绳子只剩纤维。

abstract.en: A decomposing log is a book whose pages are being returned to the library of the forest.
abstract.cn: 分解中的倒木是一本书，书页正被还给森林的图书馆。

abstract.en: When a team decomposes a task, it is rotting the workload on purpose.
abstract.cn: 当团队拆分任务时，他们是在有意让工作量「腐烂」掉。

examples.en: Plastic does not decompose easily, which is why it persists in the ocean.
examples.cn: 塑料不易分解，这正是它在海洋中持久存在的原因。

examples.en: The enzyme helps bacteria decompose cellulose in the rumen.
examples.cn: 这种酶帮助细菌分解瘤胃中的纤维素。

examples.en: We decompose the workflow into steps that can be tested separately.
examples.cn: 我们把工作流拆成可以分别测试的步骤。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（拆）+ compose（组成）→ 把组成拆掉 → 分解、腐烂

root: 拉丁语 de-「分开、向下」+ componere「放在一起」（com- + ponere「放置」）；经法语 décomposer 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one action: undoing a structured whole, whether by heat, microbes, mathematics, code, analysis, death or collapse.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：把有结构的整体拆开，手段可以是加热、微生物、数学、代码、分析、死亡或崩解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bonds loosening until a whole becomes simpler pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：结合逐渐松开，整体变成更简单的碎片。

branches.en: THE CORE: a compound or a dead body comes apart into simpler substances.
branches.cn: 核心：化合物或尸体拆解为更简单的物质。

branches.en: THE AGENT: a subject can make the breakdown happen, shifting the verb to transitive use.
branches.cn: 施动者：主语可使分解发生，动词由此转为及物用法。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: mathematics and computing split objects and tasks by design.
branches.cn: 结构：数学与计算按设计把对象和任务拆开。

branches.en: THE TEXT: an argument is taken apart into claims and assumptions.
branches.cn: 文本：论证被拆成主张与假设。

branches.en: THE END: a body passes through post-mortem stages, and an institution loses its internal bonds.
branches.cn: 终点：尸体经历死后阶段，机构失去内部纽带。

intro.en: Decompose is a reversal prefix on a verb of putting together.
intro.cn: decompose 是在「组合」动词上加表反转的前缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements are de- 'apart' and ponere 'place', the second reached through French composer rather than direct Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 成分是 de-「分开」与 ponere「放置」，后者经法语 composer 而非直接从拉丁语进入。

items.example: A decomposer returns nutrients to the soil.
items.exampleCN: 分解者把养分归还土壤。

items.example: The material is decomposable within one season.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料一个季节内即可分解。
若干物种构成了这个群落。

items.example: The position of the log affects how it decomposes.
items.exampleCN: 倒木的位置会影响它的分解方式。

items.example: The flood deposited silt over the floodplain.
items.exampleCN: 洪水在泛滥平原上沉积了淤泥。

items.example: The new rule imposes a cost on polluters.
items.exampleCN: 新规给污染者施加了成本。

definition_zh: 放射性衰变；不稳定原子核自发转变为另一种核并放出辐射的过程
definition_en: the spontaneous transformation of an unstable atomic nucleus into another nucleus, accompanied by the emission of particles or rays
core_image: 一排灯逐盏熄灭，每灭一盏就留下一点余热，而熄灭的节奏始终不变
scene: 探测器旁的样品每发生一次衰变，计数就增加一格。 Every radioactive decay in the sample added one more count to the detector.
sceneCN: 这里 radioactive decay 指「不稳定核自发转变并放出辐射的过程」（第 1 个义项：原子核自发改变化学身份的过程）；句意：样品中每一次放射性衰变，都让探测器的计数增加一格。图中可辨识物件：样品盒、探测器、计数刻度、屏蔽层。

pos.zh: 放射性衰变（可数或不可数）

senses.title: The nuclear transformation itself
senses.titleCN: 原子核自身的转变过程
senses.definition: the process by which an unstable nucleus changes into a different nucleus and emits radiation
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定原子核变成另一种原子核并放出辐射的过程
senses.example: Radioactive decay turns uranium into a long series of lighter nuclei.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性衰变把铀变成一长串更轻的核。
senses.why: Decay here keeps the old image of falling away, applied to a nucleus that cannot hold its present form.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「衰」保留了旧有的「落下、消减」意象，只是用在了一个维持不住现有形态的原子核上。

senses.title: A single decay event
senses.definition: one individual act of transformation by one nucleus at one moment
senses.definitionCN: 某一个原子核在某一时刻发生的一次转变
senses.example: Each radioactive decay releases a fixed amount of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次放射性衰变都放出固定数量的能量。
senses.why: The process is countable at the level of single nuclei, so the same phrase names one event as well as the whole phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程在单个核的层面可数，因此同一短语既指整体现象，也指一次事件。

senses.title: The rate and the half-life
senses.definition: the predictable speed at which a sample decays, expressed as a half-life
senses.definitionCN: 样品衰变的可预测速度，以半衰期表示
senses.example: The rate of radioactive decay does not change with temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性衰变的速率不随温度改变。
senses.why: Because each nucleus decays at random but the population follows a fixed curve, the rate became the measurable face of the process.
senses.whyCN: 单个核的衰变随机，整体却遵循固定曲线，因此速率成了这个过程可测量的一面。

senses.title: A particular mode of decay
senses.definition: one of the routes a nucleus can take, such as alpha, beta or gamma emission
senses.definitionCN: 原子核可走的某条路径，如放出阿尔法、贝塔或伽马射线
senses.example: Beta decay changes a neutron into a proton inside the nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 贝塔衰变使核内的一个中子变成一个质子。
senses.why: Different nuclei fall apart in different ways, and each route is called a mode of the same general process.
senses.whyCN: 不同的核以不同方式解体，每条路径都称为同一总过程的某种模式。

senses.title: A chain of successive decays
senses.definition: a series in which each decay product is itself unstable and decays in turn
senses.definitionCN: 每一个衰变产物自身也不稳定、继续衰变的序列
senses.example: The decay chain ends only when a stable lead isotope is reached.
senses.exampleCN: 这条衰变链直到抵达稳定的铅同位素才结束。
senses.why: One fall makes the next possible, so the process is naturally described as a chain rather than a single step.
senses.whyCN: 一次下落使下一次成为可能，因此这个过程天然被描述成链，而不是单步。

senses.title: The natural clock for dating
senses.definition: the use of a known decay rate to calculate the age of a rock or a once-living object
senses.definitionCN: 利用已知衰变速率计算岩石或曾存活物体的年龄
senses.example: Carbon dating depends on the radioactive decay of a rare isotope.
senses.exampleCN: 碳定年依赖一种稀有同位素的放射性衰变。
senses.why: A constant rate turns the remaining amount into a record of elapsed time, so the process doubles as a clock.
senses.whyCN: 恒定的速率使剩余量成为流逝时间的记录，因此这个过程兼作时钟。

senses.title: Heat from falling nuclei
senses.definition: the warmth produced inside the Earth or a waste container by ongoing decay
senses.definitionCN: 地球内部或废物容器中因持续衰变而产生的热
senses.example: Radioactive decay keeps the planet's interior warm.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性衰变使行星内部保持温热。
senses.why: Each decay releases energy that becomes heat, so the process is also an internal furnace.
senses.whyCN: 每次衰变都放出会变成热的能量，因此这个过程也是一座内部熔炉。

senses.title: The counted signature in a detector
senses.titleCN: 探测器里被计数的信号
senses.definition: the individual clicks or counts by which an instrument records that decay is happening
senses.definitionCN: 仪器借以记录衰变正在发生的单次咔嗒或计数
senses.example: The detector logged one radioactive decay every few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器每隔几秒就记录到一次放射性衰变。
senses.why: What an instrument can actually see is a count, so the abstract process is also named by its smallest observable sign.
senses.whyCN: 仪器真正能看到的只是一次计数，因此这个抽象过程也用它最小的可观测迹象来称呼。

intro.en: Radioactive decay combines the ray-and-activity compound with decay, from Latin decadere 'to fall away'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: radioactive decay 把「射线—活动」复合词与 decay 结合，而 decay 出自拉丁 decadere「落下、消减」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cadere meant 'to fall', and it supplies the falling image in decay, accident and cadence.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」，为 decay、accident、cadence 提供了「下落」的意象。

items.en: De- 'down, away' plus cadere produced decadere, 'to fall away, to sink', the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 「向下、离开」加「落下」构成 decadere，意为「落走、下沉」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French decair carried the word into English, where it first described rotting matter or declining fortunes.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，最初描述腐烂之物或衰败的境遇。

items.en: When unstable nuclei were found to change spontaneously, the old word for falling away described the change without implying any outside cause.
items.cn: 当不稳定核被发现会自行变化时，这个表示「落走」的旧词正好描述这种变化，且不暗示任何外因。

items.en: Twentieth-century geology added decay chains, decay heat and decay products as the process became a tool and a heat source.
items.cn: 二十世纪的地质学又添了衰变链、衰变热与衰变产物，这个过程成了工具与热源。

items.en: The first written uses of the exact phrase are approximate; the Latin chain is well attested.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的书证年代为约数；拉丁语链条有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds fall-root words and one term that only looks related; group two holds words for the splitting and the timing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「落下」词根的词与一个只是看起来相关的术语；第二组是关于分裂与计时的词。

entries.definition: The bare verb or noun for falling away, used of teeth, buildings and nuclei alike; the physics phrase narrows it to nuclei.
entries.definitionCN: 表示落下、消减的动词或名词，可用于牙齿、建筑与原子核；物理短语把它收窄到核。

entries.definition: From the same falling-away stock: a decline in standards or morals, with no physics involved.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「落走」词源：指标准或道德的衰退，与物理无关。

entries.definition: Built on the same falling verb: trees whose leaves fall each year, a literal use of the old image.
entries.definitionCN: 构于同一个「落下」动词：指每年落叶的树，是旧意象的字面用法。

entries.definition: Probably from Dutch or another source meaning a lure; it is not related to the falling root despite the shared opening.
entries.definitionCN: 可能来自荷兰语或其他表示「诱饵」的来源；尽管开头相同，与「落下」词根无关。

entries.definition: The splitting of a heavy nucleus into two large parts; it is one kind of nuclear change, often triggered rather than spontaneous.
entries.definitionCN: 重核裂成两个较大部分；它是核变化的一种，常被触发而非自发。

entries.definition: The historical word for one element changing into another, which radioactive decay achieves naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 一种元素变成另一种的旧称，而放射性衰变正是自然实现这一点的方式。

entries.definition: The time needed for half a sample to decay; it is a measure of the process, not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 样品一半发生衰变所需的时间；它衡量过程，而非过程本身。

entries.definition: A general word for falling into pieces; early physics used it for decay, but it is wider and less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指碎成小块；早期物理学用它指衰变，但它更宽泛也更不精确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: radioactive 'ray-active' plus decay 'fall away': nuclei falling away while sending out rays.
normal.cn: 「射线活动的」加「落走」：原子核一边落走一边发出射线。

normal.en: The family runs decay, decayed, decay product, decay series, radioactive decay.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括衰变、已衰变的、衰变产物、衰变系列、放射性衰变。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: rate of decay, decay chain, decay heat.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：衰变速率、衰变链、衰变热。

normal.en: The same falling root appears in decadence and deciduous, both literal or social falls.
normal.cn: 同一个「落下」词根出现在「衰败」与「落叶」这两个词里，一个是社会下落，一个是字面落下。

normal.en: Half-life turns the process into a clock, which is why rocks can be dated.
normal.cn: 半衰期把过程变成时钟，岩石因此可以被定年。

abstract.en: Picture a row of lamps going out one by one at a rhythm that never changes.
abstract.cn: 想象一排灯以始终不变的节奏一盏盏熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a falling stone that leaves a little warmth each time it lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一块下落的石头，每次落地都留下一点余温。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose pendulum is a nucleus and whose ticks are clicks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，摆是原子核，滴答是计数器的咔嗒。

examples.en: Radioactive decay is unaffected by ordinary heat or pressure.
examples.cn: 放射性衰变不受普通温度或压力的影响。

examples.en: The decay chain of uranium ends in a stable isotope of lead.
examples.cn: 铀的衰变链最终止于一种稳定的铅同位素。

examples.en: Geologists date the layer by measuring radioactive decay.
examples.cn: 地质学家通过测量放射性衰变来确定这一层的年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「radioactive（放射性的）+ decay（衰败）」——一边放出射线一边衰下去，就是放射性衰变

root: radioactive（radius「射线」+ activus「活动的」）+ decay（拉丁 decadere「落走」= de-「向下」+ cadere「落下」）。英语 radioactive decay。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a nucleus falling away: the whole process, one event, its rate, its modes, its chain, its use as a clock, its heat and the single click a detector records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个落走的核展开：整个过程、一次事件、速率、方式、链条、作为时钟、作为热源，以及探测器记下的一次咔嗒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp after another going out at a fixed rhythm, each leaving a trace of warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排灯以固定节奏逐盏熄灭，每一盏都留下一点温热。

branches.en: PROCESS AND INSTANCE: the long transformation and a single nucleus's turn are the same fall at two magnifications.
branches.cn: 过程与单例：漫长的转变与某一个核的一次变化，是同一次下落的两种放大。

branches.en: THE METRONOME: random individual events add up to a fixed rate, and that rate becomes measurable.
branches.cn: 节拍器：单个事件随机，合起来却是固定速率，而这一速率变得可测。

branches.en: THE ROUTES: different nuclei take different paths, and each path leaves a product that may fall again.
branches.cn: 路径：不同的核走不同的路，每条路都留下可能再次下落的产物。

branches.en: THE TWO USES: the constant rate reads as elapsed time in rock, and as warmth in the Earth.
branches.cn: 两种用途：恒定速率在岩石里读作流逝的时间，在地球里读作温热。

branches.en: THE OBSERVABLE SIGN: what a detector can actually record is one click at a time.
branches.cn: 可观测的迹象：探测器真正能记录的，只是一次一次的咔嗒。

intro.en: The phrase joins a modern science compound to an old verb of falling, so one half is nineteenth-century and the other is Latin.
intro.cn: 这个短语把近代科学复合词接到一个古老的「落下」动词上，一半是十九世纪，一半是拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius and agere form the first word; Latin cadere and its compound decadere form the second, and cadere also yields accident, cadence and case.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 radius 与 agere 构成第一个词；拉丁 cadere 及其复合形式 decadere 构成第二个词，cadere 还衍生出 accident、cadence、case。

items.example: The ray-root begins the physics word.
items.exampleCN: 「射线」词根开启了这个物理词。

items.example: The adjective says the nucleus is at work.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说明原子核正在运作。

items.example: The verb supplies the falling image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供下落的意象。

items.example: The prefix directs the fall downward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把下落引向下方。
这个复合形式给英语提供了表示「衰败」的动词。

items.example: Wood decays faster in damp air.
items.exampleCN: 木头在潮湿空气里腐烂得更快。

items.meaning: the nucleus left after a decay
items.example: The decay product is often unstable too.
items.exampleCN: 衰变产物往往也不稳定。

items.example: The critics spoke of cultural decadence.
items.exampleCN: 批评者谈到文化的衰败。

latinEntries.structure: cadere, cado, cecidi, casum (v., third conjugation)

definition_zh: 热液喷口；海底热泉（热流体从海底裂隙喷出的开口）
definition_en: an opening on the seafloor where hot mineral-rich fluid discharges into cold seawater
core_image: 海底裂开一道缝，黑色的热水柱夹着矿物颗粒往上冲，遇冷立刻沉下一圈烟尘
scene: 深潜器悬停在裂隙上方，滚烫的黑色水流夹着矿物颗粒涌出。 A hydrothermal vent pours mineral-rich water onto the seafloor.
sceneCN: 这里 hydrothermal vent 指「海底热流体喷出的开口」（第 1 个义项：作为地点的喷口本身）；句意为一个热液喷口把富含矿物的热水倾泻到海底。

pos.zh: 热液喷口；海底热泉（可数，复数 hydrothermal vents）

derivatives.zh: vent（拉丁 ventus「风」经「出风口」义而来）→ 开口、排气口；排放
hydro-（希腊「水」）+ thermal（希腊「热」）→ 热液的：热水参与的
black（黑）+ smoker（冒烟者）→ 喷出黑色矿物颗粒的高温喷口：黑烟囱
cold（冷）+ seep（渗漏）→ 低温流体缓慢渗出的海底地点：冷泉（与热液喷口相对）

senses.title: The opening itself
senses.titleCN: 喷口本体：热流体喷出的海底开口
senses.definition: the seafloor opening through which hot fluid discharges
senses.definitionCN: 热流体由此排出的海底开口
senses.example: A hydrothermal vent pours mineral-rich water onto the seafloor.
senses.exampleCN: 一个热液喷口把富含矿物的热水倾泻到海底。
senses.why: vent names an opening, and hydrothermal names the fluid, so the phrase is literally a hot-water outlet.
senses.whyCN: vent 命名开口，hydrothermal 命名流体，短语字面就是「热水的出口」。

senses.title: The rising plume
senses.titleCN: 上升的羽流：喷出的热水柱
senses.definition: the cloud of hot particle-laden water rising from the opening
senses.definitionCN: 从开口上升的、夹带颗粒的热水云
senses.example: A dark plume rose from the hydrothermal vent.
senses.exampleCN: 一股深色羽流从热液喷口升起。
senses.why: what the vent emits is continuous with the vent, so the word is used for the plume as well as the hole.
senses.whyCN: 喷口喷出的东西与喷口连成一体，因此这个词也用来指羽流而不只指洞口。

senses.title: The chimney it builds
senses.definition: the mineral structure built up around the opening by precipitated solids
senses.definitionCN: 沉淀物在开口周围堆成的矿物构造
senses.example: The hydrothermal vent grew a chimney two metres tall.
senses.exampleCN: 这个热液喷口长出一座两米高的烟囱。
senses.why: dissolved minerals settle where hot fluid meets cold seawater, so the opening slowly builds its own tower.
senses.whyCN: 溶解矿物在热流体与冷海水相遇处沉淀，于是开口慢慢筑起自己的塔。

senses.title: A chemosynthetic community
senses.definition: the assemblage of organisms that live on chemical energy at a vent
senses.definitionCN: 依靠化学能在喷口处生活的生物集合
senses.example: Tube worms crowd around the hydrothermal vent.
senses.exampleCN: 管虫密密地围着这个热液喷口。
senses.why: the vent supplies sulphides instead of sunlight, so the word also names the unique community it feeds.
senses.whyCN: 喷口提供的是硫化物而非阳光，因此这个词也命名它供养的独特群落。

senses.title: An exit of a circulation system
senses.definition: the discharge point of a larger hydrothermal circulation
senses.definitionCN: 更大规模热液循环的排出点
senses.example: Each hydrothermal vent marks where the circuit reaches the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 每个热液喷口都标出循环回到海面处。
senses.why: in a circuit, the vent is the outlet end, so the word describes a position in a system as well as a hole.
senses.whyCN: 在一个循环里，喷口是出口端，因此这个词既描述洞口，也描述系统中的一个位置。

senses.title: An ancient vent and its ore
senses.titleCN: 古喷口与块状硫化物矿
senses.definition: a former vent preserved in rock as a massive sulphide deposit
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石中、成为块状硫化物矿床的旧喷口
senses.example: Miners worked an ancient hydrothermal vent for copper.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工开采一处古热液喷口以获取铜。
senses.why: when the seafloor is lifted onto land, the vent and its chimney become an ore body.
senses.whyCN: 当海底被抬升到陆地上，喷口与烟囱就变成了矿体。

senses.title: A target for water-column survey
senses.definition: a feature located by detecting its plume in the water column
senses.definitionCN: 通过探测水柱中的羽流而定位的对象
senses.example: The ship found a hydrothermal vent by tracing a chemical anomaly.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船通过追踪化学异常找到了一处热液喷口。
senses.why: the vent is hidden below, but its plume spreads above, so survey work treats the plume as the vent's signature.
senses.whyCN: 喷口藏在下面，羽流却扩散在上面，因此探测工作把羽流当作喷口的签名。

senses.title: An analogue on icy moons
senses.definition: a hypothetical seafloor vent beneath the ice of another world
senses.definitionCN: 其他天体冰层之下假想的海底喷口
senses.example: A hydrothermal vent under that ice could support life.
senses.exampleCN: 那片冰下的热液喷口可能支持生命。
senses.why: the conditions are defined by physics rather than by Earth, so planetary science reuses the term for alien oceans.
senses.whyCN: 这些条件由物理而非地球决定，因此行星科学把这个词用于外星海洋。

intro.en: Hydrothermal vent joins a Greek-rooted adjective to an English noun of Latin origin. Vent goes back through Old French to Latin ventus 'wind', whose sense shifted from moving air to the hole it blows through. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydrothermal vent 把希腊词根的形容词接在一个拉丁语源的英语名词上。vent 经古法语上溯拉丁 ventus「风」，词义从流动的空气转为它吹过的孔洞。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ventus meant 'wind'; Old French vent carried both 'wind' and 'opening for air', and English borrowed the latter.
items.cn: ventus 意为「风」；古法语 vent 兼有「风」与「通气口」两义，英语借入的是后者。

items.en: Hydro- and thermal come from Greek hydor 'water' and therme 'heat', joined in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: hydro- 与 thermal 来自希腊 hydor「水」与 therme「热」，于十九世纪合成。

items.en: The phrase hydrothermal vent was assembled in the late twentieth century once seafloor hot springs were directly observed.
items.cn: 海底热泉被直接观测到之后，hydrothermal vent 这一短语才在二十世纪后期组合起来。

items.en: Sailors' slang for a smoky funnel was borrowed for the dark chimneys, producing the informal synonym black smoker.
items.cn: 水手把冒烟的烟囱称作黑烟囱，这一俚语被借来形容深色喷口，产生了非正式同义词 black smoker。

items.en: The discovery of vent communities in 1977 made the phrase a biological term as well as a geological one.
items.cn: 一九七七年喷口生物群落的发现，使这个短语同时成为生物学术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the two elements are secure, but the earliest use of the exact phrase is not fixed in reference works.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个成分都可靠，但这一确切短语的最早使用在各类工具书中并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the vent types and related discharge features that are routinely confused; group two holds the general words for an opening or a spring.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的喷口类型与相关排放地貌；第二组是泛指开口或泉的词语。

entries.definition: A very hot vent whose fluid precipitates dark metal sulphides; it is a kind of hydrothermal vent, not a separate thing.
entries.definitionCN: 流体沉淀出深色金属硫化物的极热喷口；它是热液喷口的一种，并非另类事物。

entries.definition: A cooler vent whose fluid precipitates pale silica and barytes rather than dark sulphides.
entries.definitionCN: 温度较低的喷口，流体沉淀浅色硅质与重晶石，而非深色硫化物。

entries.definition: A seafloor seep of cold, often methane-rich fluid; it lacks the high temperature that defines a hydrothermal vent.
entries.definitionCN: 低温且常富含甲烷的海底渗漏；缺少定义热液喷口所需的高温。

entries.definition: A cluster of vents and deposits in one area; a single opening is a vent, not a field.
entries.definitionCN: 同一区域的一组喷口与沉积；单个开口是喷口，不是热液场。

entries.definition: Any opening for air, gas or liquid; alone it says nothing about temperature or the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 任何供气、气或液体通过的开口；单用时不涉及温度或海洋。

entries.definition: A natural flow of water from the ground; it is usually on land and usually cool.
entries.definitionCN: 水从地下自然流出；通常在陆上，通常温度不高。

entries.definition: A slow, spreading flow through pores or small cracks; it stresses gradual leakage, not forceful discharge.
entries.definitionCN: 经孔隙或小裂缝缓慢扩散的流动；强调渐渗，而非猛烈喷出。

entries.definition: The rising cloud carried away from the opening; it is the product of a vent, not the vent itself.
entries.definitionCN: 从开口被带走的上升云团；它是喷口的产物，不是喷口本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real vent types and real physical steps, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词、真实的喷口类型与真实的物理步骤，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: hydrothermal is water plus heat; vent is an opening: the phrase is a hot-water opening.
normal.cn: hydrothermal 是水加热，vent 是开口：这个短语就是「热水的开口」。

normal.en: Dark smoke means dark ore: black smokers precipitate sulphides, white smokers precipitate silica.
normal.cn: 深色的烟意味着深色的矿：黑烟囱沉淀硫化物，白烟囱沉淀硅质。

normal.en: A vent is hot, a seep is cold: the two words divide seafloor discharge by temperature.
normal.cn: 喷口是热的，渗漏是冷的：两个词按温度划分海底排放。

normal.en: The chimney is made by the vent itself, layer by layer, where hot meets cold.
normal.cn: 烟囱是喷口自己在热水遇冷处一层层造出来的。

normal.en: No sunlight, no problem: the community runs on sulphides through chemosynthesis.
normal.cn: 没有阳光也没关系：这个群落靠硫化物进行化能合成。

abstract.en: A vent is a wound in the seafloor that keeps talking.
abstract.cn: 喷口是海底的一道伤口，一直在说话。

abstract.en: It is a chimney with no fire below, only stone and hot water arguing.
abstract.cn: 它是一座下面没有火的烟囱，只有石头与热水在争论。

abstract.en: Life here begins with chemistry instead of dawn.
abstract.cn: 这里的生命以化学开始，而不是以黎明开始。

examples.en: The submersible filmed a hydrothermal vent at two thousand metres.
examples.cn: 深潜器在两千公尺处拍摄到一处热液喷口。

examples.en: Each hydrothermal vent hosts its own community of worms and clams.
examples.cn: 每个热液喷口都养育着自己的一套蠕虫与蛤类群落。

examples.en: The hydrothermal vent built a chimney of metal sulphides.
examples.cn: 这个热液喷口用金属硫化物筑起一座烟囱。

dict_mnemonic.text: hydrothermal（热液的）+ vent（出口）＝热液喷口；热水从海底裂缝冲出，遇冷沉淀成烟囱，养活靠化学能的生命。

root: hydrothermal（希腊 hydor「水」+ therme「热」）+ vent（拉丁 ventus「风」，义转为出风口）；短语为二十世纪后期地质学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one opening: the hole, the plume, the chimney, the community it feeds, its place in a circuit, its fossil ore, its plume as a survey signature, and its analogue on icy moons.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个开口展开：洞口、羽流、烟囱、它供养的群落、它在循环中的位置、它化成的矿、作为探测信号的羽流，以及冰卫星上的类比。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack in the seafloor sending a hot dark jet into cold water.
core.cn: 核心意象：海底一道裂缝，把滚烫的深色水柱送进冷水里。

branches.en: HOLE AND JET: the opening, then what comes out of it.
branches.cn: 洞口与射流：先是开口，再是从中出来的东西。

branches.en: BUILT TOWER: precipitation turns the opening into a structure.
branches.cn: 堆成的塔：沉淀把开口变成构造。

branches.en: COMMUNITY AND CIRCUIT: what lives there, and where the outlet sits in the loop.
branches.cn: 群落与循环：那里住着什么，以及出口在环流中的位置。

branches.en: ORE AND SIGNATURE: a fossil vent becomes a mine, a plume becomes a clue.
branches.cn: 矿与信号：化石喷口变成矿，羽流变成线索。

branches.en: ALIEN ANALOGUE: the same opening imagined under another world's ice.
branches.cn: 外星类比：同一个开口被想象在另一个天体的冰下。

intro.en: Hydrothermal vent combines a Greek-rooted adjective with a short English noun, so the phrase is morphologically transparent at both ends.
intro.cn: hydrothermal vent 把希腊词根的形容词与一个简短英语名词组合，短语两端在构词上都透明。

latinIntro.en: Hydrothermal contributes no Latin entry; vent does, through Latin ventus 'wind'. The two halves come from different language families.
latinIntro.cn: hydrothermal 不提供拉丁条目；vent 则经拉丁 ventus「风」提供。两半来自不同语系。

items.exampleCN: hydro- 是形容词 hydrothermal 的开头。
therme 提供 thermal 与 thermometer。

items.structure: ventus, venti (Latin noun, masculine, fourth declension)
items.example: Ventus gave French vent and English vent.
items.exampleCN: ventus 给出法语 vent 与英语 vent。

items.structure: vent (English noun from Old French vent)
items.meaning: an opening for air or fluid
items.meaningCN: 供空气或流体通过的开口
items.exampleCN: 蒸汽从一个排气口逸出。

items.meaning: relating to hot water in rock

items.exampleCN: 这个热液喷口排出硫化物。

items.meaning: a hot vent with dark precipitate
items.meaningCN: 沉淀物呈深色的高温喷口
items.example: The black smoker chimney stood three metres high.

items.meaning: a cooler vent with pale precipitate
items.meaningCN: 沉淀物呈浅色的较低温喷口
items.example: A white smoker stood beside the black one.
items.exampleCN: 一座白烟囱立在黑烟囱旁边。

items.example: Methane supports life at the cold seep.
items.exampleCN: 甲烷在冷泉处供养生命。

items.example: The plume drifted west from the vent.

definition_zh: 有损声誉的；令人难堪的；危及安全的；（罕）愿意让步的
definition_en: revealing something damaging or exposing someone to risk, and rarely, willing to settle by concession
core_image: 一张被拍到的照片，桌上摊着本不该出现的文件
scene: 记者的相机里有一段录像，画面中的人正把一份本不该带出的文件放回包里。 The newspaper refused to publish the compromising photographs until the case was closed.
sceneCN: 这里 compromising 指「一旦公开就会损害当事人声誉」（第 1 个义项：有损名誉的）；句意为报社拒绝在案件了结之前发表那些令人难堪的照片。可辨识物件：相机、录像画面、文件、公文包。

pos.zh: 有损声誉的；令人难堪的
危及安全的；削弱主张的
（罕）愿意让步的

collocations.zh: 一旦曝光就难堪的处境
在政治上会带来麻烦的

derivatives.zh: 以损害声誉的方式（罕用）

senses.title: Damaging to a reputation
senses.titleCN: 有损名誉、一旦公开就难堪
senses.definition: of a photograph, letter or fact, likely to bring a person into discredit if known
senses.definitionCN: 指照片、信件或事实一旦被人知道，就可能使某人名誉受损
senses.example: The newspaper refused to publish the compromising photographs until the case was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 报社拒绝在案件了结之前发表那些令人难堪的照片。
senses.why: the participle inherits the verb's risk sense: what compromises a person is compromising.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词继承了动词的「风险」义：会危及某人的东西，就是 compromising。

senses.title: Incriminating in substance
senses.titleCN: 内容本身构成不利证据
senses.definition: of a document or a recording, containing material that suggests wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 指文件或录音中含有暗示不当行为的材料
senses.example: The auditors found compromising entries in the ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员在账簿里发现了不利的条目。
senses.why: reputation damage and legal exposure overlap: the same paper can end a career and start a case.
senses.whyCN: 名誉受损与法律风险彼此重叠：同一张纸可以毁掉前程，也可以开出一桩案子。

senses.title: Risky for security
senses.definition: of a practice or a fault, likely to weaken a system's protection
senses.definitionCN: 指某种做法或缺陷可能削弱系统的防护
senses.example: A compromising default setting left the server open.
senses.exampleCN: 一个危及安全的默认设置让服务器敞开了。
senses.why: the engineering branch of compromise produces an adjective for whatever introduces the weakness.
senses.whyCN: compromise 在工程上的那一支，造出一个形容词，用来指任何引入弱点的东西。

senses.title: Weakening a case in argument
senses.definition: of a fact or an admission, tending to make a claim less credible
senses.definitionCN: 指某事实或某项承认，会使某个主张的可信度下降
senses.example: The delay was compromising for the whole theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这段延迟对整个理论都构成削弱。
senses.why: a case is like a structure: it can be undermined by one weak point, and the adjective marks that point.
senses.whyCN: 一个论点就像一座结构：一个薄弱点就能把它掏空，这个形容词标记的正是那个点。

senses.title: Awkward if seen
senses.titleCN: 被人看见就会解释不清的处境
senses.definition: of a position or a meeting, hard to explain and therefore embarrassing
senses.definitionCN: 指某种处境或会面难以解释，因而令人尴尬
senses.example: They were found in a compromising position in the archive room.
senses.exampleCN: 有人发现他们在档案室里，情形很难解释清楚。
senses.why: this is the reputation sense narrowed to a scene rather than a document.
senses.whyCN: 这是名誉义收窄到「一个场面」，而非一份文件。

senses.title: Willing to give ground
senses.definition: of a person or a mood, ready to settle by concession rather than insist
senses.definitionCN: 指人或情绪愿意以让步了结，而不坚持到底
senses.example: A compromising tone in the letter suggested room to negotiate.
senses.exampleCN: 信里那种肯商量的语气，暗示还有谈的余地。
senses.why: the rare adjective reading is the plain one: showing a disposition to compromise.
senses.whyCN: 这个罕见的形容词义其实最直白：显示出愿意妥协的倾向。

senses.title: Harmful to trust
senses.definition: of a disclosure or a rumour, likely to damage a relationship between people or bodies
senses.definitionCN: 指某项披露或传言可能损害个人或机构之间的信任关系
senses.example: The rumour was compromising for both governments.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传言对两国政府都有损害。
senses.why: trust is a shared asset, so anything that weakens it is compromising to both holders.
senses.whyCN: 信任是双方共有的资产，削弱它的东西，对两边都构成损害。

senses.title: Lowering a standard
senses.definition: of a shortcut or a revision, reducing the quality that a thing was meant to have
senses.definitionCN: 指某种捷径或修改，降低了事物本应具备的品质
senses.example: The cheaper alloy was compromising for the whole design.
senses.exampleCN: 那种更便宜的合金拖累了整个设计。
senses.why: the engineering sense of a diluted standard, dressed as an adjective for the cause.
senses.whyCN: 这是「标准被稀释」的工程义，以形容词形式指向那个原因。

intro.en: Compromising is the present participle of compromise, whose Latin source compromittere meant to promise mutually; the damaging sense grew in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: compromising 是 compromise 的现在分词，后者的拉丁源头 compromittere 意为「相互许诺」；指「损害」的义项在十七世纪发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, to let go', and it supplies the second half of the compound.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」，是这个复合词的后一半。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus promittere 'to promise' produced the verb for binding oneself mutually, first in arbitration.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 promittere「许诺」构成这个动词，表示相互约束，最初用于仲裁。

items.en: English developed the sense 'to expose to risk or discredit', and the participle followed, describing whatever causes that exposure.
items.cn: 英语发展出「使陷入风险或名誉受损」义，分词随后跟进，用来描述造成这种暴露的东西。

items.en: The adjective settled into phrases about papers, positions and letters, the ordinary stock of scandal and litigation.
items.cn: 这个形容词固定出现在关于文件、处境与信件的说法里，那正是丑闻与诉讼的日常材料。

items.en: Photography and then computing widened its range: a compromising picture, a compromising configuration.
items.cn: 摄影、以及后来的计算机，拓宽了它的范围：会坏事的照片、会出事的配置。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact decade when the adjective began to mean damaging is unsettled, and the further history of the sending root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个形容词开始表示「有损」的确切年代没有定论；「送出」词根更早的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb or of confusing near-forms; group two holds adjectives that also describe what harms a person or a case.
note.cn: 第一组收同一个动词的各种形式、以及容易混淆的近形词；第二组收同样描述「损害某人或某事」的形容词。

entries.definition: The past participle: already weakened or breached, describing the victim rather than the thing that did the damage.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词：已经被削弱或攻破，描述受害者，而不是造成损害的东西。

entries.definition: Built on promittere like compromise, but without com-: it means giving grounds for hope, not grounds for scandal.
entries.definitionCN: 与 compromise 同出 promittere，但没有 com-：意为「有前途」，而非「会出事」。

entries.definition: From comprehendere 'to grasp together': consisting of, a completely different verb behind a similar shape.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 comprehendere「一并抓住」：意为「包含」，相似外形背后是完全不同的动词。

entries.definition: With un-: refusing to concede, which is almost the opposite of the rare willing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 加 un-：拒绝让步，几乎与那个罕见的「愿意让步」义相反。

entries.definition: Showing that someone is guilty of a crime; it covers only the evidence branch of compromising.
entries.definitionCN: 显示某人有罪；只覆盖 compromising 的证据那一支。

entries.definition: Causing awkwardness; it names the feeling, while compromising names the damage that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 造成尴尬；它命名的是感受，而 compromising 命名的是随之而来的损害。

entries.definition: Causing harm of any kind; the widest of the group, with no hint of scandal or security.
entries.definitionCN: 造成任何种类的伤害；本组中范围最广，不带丑闻或安全的暗示。

entries.definition: Bringing shame on a person; it judges conduct, whereas compromising judges the exposure of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人蒙羞；它评判行为，而 compromising 评判证据被暴露的风险。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the verb's present participle, so it names the thing that does the compromising.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是动词的现在分词，因此它命名的是「造成损害的那一方」。

normal.en: The family runs compromise, compromising, compromised, uncompromising, compromiser.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compromise、compromising、compromised、uncompromising、compromiser。

normal.en: Fixed phrases are mostly about paper and scenes: compromising letters, a compromising position.
normal.cn: 固定搭配多与纸面与场面有关：会坏事的信件、难以解释的处境。

normal.en: The negative uncompromising means the opposite: refusing to yield.
normal.cn: 否定的 uncompromising 意为相反：拒绝让步。

normal.en: The related promising shares the promise root but means hopeful, not damaging.
normal.cn: 近形的 promising 同出「许诺」词根，却意为「有前途」，而非「有损」。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph taken at the worst possible moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在最不该按下快门时拍下的照片。

abstract.en: Picture a single loose thread that unravels a whole sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象一根松线把整只袖子拆开。

abstract.en: Picture a key left in a lock overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙整夜留在锁孔里。

examples.en: The minister resigned after compromising letters reached the press.
examples.cn: 那些不利的信件落到媒体手里之后，部长辞职了。

examples.en: No compromising detail was left in the shared folder.
examples.cn: 共享文件夹里没有留下任何会坏事的细节。

examples.en: The report called the loophole compromising for the whole safety system.
examples.cn: 报告称这个漏洞危及整个安全体系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「compromise（危及）+ ing」——正在危及名声的那种 → 有损声誉的

root: compromise 的现在分词；compromise 出自拉丁 compromittere「相互许诺」= com-（共同）+ promittere（许诺）；十七世纪发展出「使陷入风险、使名誉受损」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a thing that does damage on exposure: to a name, a case, a system, an argument, a scene, a trust, a standard, or, in the rare reading, a willingness to yield.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「一旦暴露就造成损害」的东西：对名声、案件、系统、论点、场面、信任、标准，或在罕见的读法里，对「愿意让步」的性格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a photograph taken at the worst possible moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：在最不该按下快门的那一刻拍下的一张照片。

branches.en: WHAT THE PAPER DOES: a photograph shames, and a ledger entry incriminates.
branches.cn: 纸面所做的事：照片使人难堪，账簿条目成为罪证。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND STANDARDS: a default setting opens a server, a cheap alloy drags the design down.
branches.cn: 系统与标准：一个默认设置敞开服务器，一种廉价合金拖累设计。

branches.en: ARGUMENTS AND TRUST: a delay weakens a theory, a rumour weakens a relationship.
branches.cn: 论点与信任：一段延迟削弱理论，一则传言削弱关系。

branches.en: THE SCENE: reputation damage narrowed to a moment someone walked in on.
branches.cn: 场面：名誉受损收窄到「有人正好撞见」的一刻。

branches.en: THE RARE READING: the same form can still mean simply ready to concede.
branches.cn: 罕见的读法：同一形式仍可只表示「愿意让步」。

intro.en: Compromising is a participle built on a Latin compound verb, so its prefix, root and ending all carry readable meaning.
intro.cn: compromising 是一个建立在拉丁复合动词上的分词，前缀、词根与词尾都带着可读的意义。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere gives promise, compromise, permit and transmit; com- adds togetherness and -ing adds the ongoing or causative reading.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 promise、compromise、permit 与 transmit；com- 增添「共同」，-ing 增添「正在进行或致成」的读法。

items.example: The prefix makes the promise mutual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使许诺成为相互的。

items.example: The root supplies the sending image.
The word sends a pledge forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把承诺送向前方。

items.meaning: to settle, to expose to risk
items.exampleCN: 一封邮件危及了那些文件。

items.example: The ending makes the verb describe a cause.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使动词转而描述一个成因。

items.example: His uncompromising reply ended the exchange.
items.exampleCN: 他毫不让步的答复终止了往来。

definition_zh: 无色的；消色差的；非彩色的
definition_en: free of colour, or designed to be free of the colour distortion in lenses
core_image: 被抽走全部颜色的灰色世界
scene: 验光师把两片薄镜叠在一起，桌上的图纸只剩明暗深浅。 The optician used an achromatic lens to remove the rainbow fringes around the image.
sceneCN: 这里 achromatic 是「消色差的」（第 2 个义项：光学上消除色差）；句意是验光师用消色差透镜去掉图像边缘的彩边。

pos.zh: 无色的；消色差的

derivatives.zh: 由本词截短构成，义为「消色差透镜；全色盲者」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「消色差性；色盲」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「无色地；以消色差方式」

senses.title: Having no colour
senses.definition: without colour, showing only black, white, and shades of grey
senses.definitionCN: 没有颜色，只呈现黑、白与深浅不同的灰
senses.example: The X-ray film showed an achromatic world of bones and shadows.
senses.exampleCN: X 光片呈现出只有骨骼与阴影的无色世界。
senses.why: Greek chroma means colour, and the negative a- strips it away; what is left is shape without hue.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 chroma 意为「颜色」，否定前缀 a- 把它抽走，剩下的只是没有色相的形状。

senses.title: Correcting colour distortion in optics
senses.definition: of a lens or optical system, designed so that colours come to the same focus and no rainbow edges appear
senses.definitionCN: 指透镜或光学系统经过设计，使各色光聚于同一焦点，不出现彩色边缘
senses.example: The achromatic doublet sharpened the telescope image dramatically.
senses.exampleCN: 消色差双合透镜显著锐化了望远镜的成像。
senses.why: If the colour has been taken away from the error, the lens no longer splits light into stray rainbow fringes.
senses.whyCN: 把「颜色」从误差里抽走之后，透镜便不再把光拆成四散的彩边。

senses.title: Free of colour in biology or chemistry
senses.definition: not staining, or lacking the usual colouring matter, as in certain cells or tissues
senses.definitionCN: （细胞、组织等）不着色的，或缺乏正常色素的
senses.example: The lab noted an achromatic region in the stained sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在染色样本里记录到一块不着色区域。
senses.why: Stains are dyes; where the dye finds nothing to hold, the picture stays colourless.
senses.whyCN: 染料就是给结构上色的东西；染料无处附着之处，画面便保持无色。

intro.en: A Greek negative prefix meets the Greek word for colour.
intro.cn: 一个希腊否定前缀遇上希腊语里表示「颜色」的词。

items.en: *ghrewg- is generally reconstructed as relating to colour or complexion; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ghrewg- 与颜色、肤色相关；更早来源不确定。

items.en: chroma meant colour, the surface tint of skin or of things.
items.cn: 希腊语 chroma 意为颜色，指皮肤或物体的表面色泽。

items.en: achromatos added the negative a-, meaning colourless.
items.cn: 希腊语 achromatos 加否定前缀 a-，意为无色的。

items.en: scientific Latin achromaticus was coined for optics in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪科学拉丁语造出 achromaticus，用于光学。

items.en: achromatic settled into optics, biology, and printing, all meaning colour has been removed.
items.cn: achromatic 落定于光学、生物与印刷领域，都指颜色被移除。

note.en: The first group is the chroma family; the second gathers words for worlds without colour.
note.cn: 第一组是 chroma 词族；第二组收集无色世界的相关词。

entries.definition: having only one colour or shades of one colour
entries.definitionCN: 单色的；一色深浅变化的

entries.definition: having many colours
entries.definitionCN: 多色的；五彩的

entries.definition: relating to colour, or with colour present
entries.definitionCN: 有色的；与颜色有关的

entries.definition: a performer of gymnastic feats; it merely sounds similar and comes from another root
entries.definitionCN: 杂技演员；只是读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: without colour, plain or dull
entries.definitionCN: 无色的；平淡乏味的

entries.definition: in one colour, especially black and white
entries.definitionCN: 单色的（尤指黑白）

entries.definition: low in colour intensity
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的；颜色淡的

entries.definition: dull and lacking brightness
entries.definitionCN: 暗淡乏味的

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Greek colour word and the negative prefix that removes it.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆点围绕希腊语的「颜色」及把它取消的否定前缀。

normal.en: a- means without, chroma means colour: achromatic is colourless.
normal.cn: a- 表示「无」，chroma 表示「颜色」：achromatic 即无色。

normal.en: chromatic is the positive partner: with colour.
normal.cn: chromatic 是它的正面对照：有色的。

normal.en: monochromatic adds mono-, one: a single colour only.
normal.cn: monochromatic 再加 mono-（一）：只剩一种颜色。

normal.en: in optics an achromatic lens stops the rainbow fringing.
normal.cn: 光学里消色差透镜能止住彩虹色的边缘。

normal.en: photography calls plain black and white scenes achromatic.
normal.cn: 摄影里纯黑白画面被称为非彩色。

abstract.en: Picture a film where someone bleached every frame grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一部被逐帧漂成灰色的影片。

abstract.en: See a lens split light into a rainbow, then a second lens pulling the colours back together.
abstract.cn: 想象一片透镜把光拆成彩虹，另一片把颜色重新收拢。

abstract.en: Feel a room drained of hue, only outlines and shadows left.
abstract.cn: 体会一间被抽掉色相的房间，只剩轮廓与影子。

examples.en: Achromatic prints hung on the wall: only black, white and grey.
examples.cn: 墙上挂的是非彩色照片：只有黑、白与灰。

examples.en: The telescope improved sharply after the maker fitted an achromatic lens.
examples.cn: 装上消色差透镜后，望远镜的成像大幅改善。

examples.en: Patients with achromatic vision see the world as shades of grey.
examples.cn: 全色盲患者眼中的世界只有深浅不一的灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克罗马提克」——阿克把「罗」（彩色）都抹掉，画面只剩黑白灰。

root: 希腊语 achromatos（无色的）由否定前缀 a-（无）与 chroma（颜色）构成；十八世纪光学借科学拉丁语 achromaticus 造词，指消除色差的透镜。

sensesIntro.en: One act of removing colour serves three fields: plain vision, corrected optics, and unstained tissue.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「抽走颜色」的动作服务三个领域：纯粹的视觉、被校正的光学、以及不着色的组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: colour lifted out, leaving only light and dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：颜色被提起抽走，只剩明与暗。

branches.en: black, white and grey as the residue of colour removed
branches.cn: 颜色被移除后剩下的黑、白与灰

branches.en: lenses that pull every colour to one focus
branches.cn: 把各色光聚到同一焦点的透镜

branches.en: tissues that refuse the dye and stay pale
branches.cn: 拒绝染料、保持苍白的组织

branches.en: removing unwanted colour, whether in an image or in an error
branches.cn: 无论在图像还是误差里，都 unwanted 地移除颜色

branches.en: the neutral world left when hue is gone
branches.cn: 色相消失后剩下的中性世界

intro.en: A Greek negative, a colour root, and scientific endings build the family.
intro.cn: 希腊否定前缀、颜色词根与科学后缀构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: The colour root chroma is Greek, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: 颜色词根 chroma 出自希腊语，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 使多样化；分散投资；开展多元化业务
definition_en: to make something more varied, or to spread money or activity across different areas
core_image: 一只手把同一种东西撒向好几块不同的田地
scene: 一家只卖一种农产品的家族企业决定把业务扩展到食品加工与乡村旅店。 The family firm decided to diversify into food processing and rural tourism.
sceneCN: 这里指「把业务扩展到新的领域」，对应第 3 个义项：企业进入与原业务不同的产品线；句意为这家家族企业决定向食品加工与乡村旅游业多元化。画面要点：农田、加工车间、旅店招牌。

pos.zh: 使多样化；分散（投资）；开展多元化业务；增加（作物、来源等的）种类

derivatives.zh: 分散风险者；多元化经营者

senses.title: To make more varied
senses.definition: to introduce a wider range of types into something
senses.definitionCN: 把更广泛的类型引入某事物
senses.example: The school diversified its reading list.
senses.exampleCN: 学校使阅读书单更加多样。
senses.why: The verb is the general action behind the noun: one line of things is turned into several lines.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是名词背后的一般动作：一条线上的一类东西被转成好几条线。

senses.title: To spread investments
senses.definition: to put money into several assets instead of one
senses.definitionCN: 把钱投入多项资产而不是只投一项
senses.example: Retirees should diversify before markets turn.
senses.exampleCN: 退休者应在市场转向之前先分散投资。
senses.why: Finance turns the general act into risk management: many assets mean many chances instead of one.
senses.whyCN: 金融把这个一般动作变成风险管理：多项资产意味着多个机会而不是一个。

senses.title: To enter new lines of business
senses.definition: for a company, to expand into products or services beyond its original line
senses.definitionCN: 企业扩展到原业务之外的产品或服务
senses.example: The chain diversified into coffee shops.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁企业扩展到咖啡店业务。
senses.why: A firm that adds a second line is literally adding kinds to its basket of revenue.
senses.whyCN: 增添第二条业务线的公司，实际上是在其收入篮子里加上新的种类。

senses.title: To vary products or markets
senses.definition: to change the mix of goods sold or the markets served
senses.definitionCN: 改变所售商品或所服务市场的组合
senses.example: The exporter diversified its markets across Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 这家出口商在亚洲各地分散市场。
senses.why: Here the added kinds are goods and destinations, so the verb shifts from entering a line to changing the mix.
senses.whyCN: 这里增添的种类是商品与目的地，动词因此从「进入一条线」转为「改变组合」。

senses.title: To broaden an economy
senses.definition: to reduce a region's dependence on one industry
senses.definitionCN: 降低一个地区对单一产业的依赖
senses.example: The province diversified away from timber.
senses.exampleCN: 该省从木材业转向多元化。
senses.why: The verb scales a company strategy up to a whole region: one industry is replaced by several.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把企业策略放大到整个地区：一个产业被好几个产业取代。

senses.title: To increase genetic variety
senses.definition: to widen the range of genes in a population or crop
senses.definitionCN: 扩大种群或作物的基因范围
senses.example: Plant breeders diversify wheat to resist disease.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者使小麦多样化以抗病。
senses.why: Breeding uses the same act without markets: more kinds in the gene pool mean fewer total failures.
senses.whyCN: 育种在没有市场的情况下使用同一动作：基因库里种类更多，整体失败就更少。

senses.title: To expand one's range of activity
senses.definition: for a person or group, to take on new kinds of work or interest
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体承担新的工作或兴趣种类
senses.example: She diversified her practice to include family law.
senses.exampleCN: 她扩展业务范围，纳入了家庭法。
senses.why: A career or practice can be a portfolio of activities, so the verb applies to a person's bundle of work.
senses.whyCN: 职业或业务可以是一组活动，因此这个动词也能用于一个人的工作束。

senses.title: To grow several crops
senses.definition: to replace a single crop with several on the same farm
senses.definitionCN: 在同一农场上以多种作物取代单一作物
senses.example: The cooperative diversified into fruit and nuts.
senses.exampleCN: 合作社多样化种植水果与坚果。
senses.why: The field is the simplest basket: several crops spread the risk of weather and price.
senses.whyCN: 田地是最简单的篮子：几种作物分散天气与价格风险。

senses.title: To change the mix of sources
senses.definition: to add different sources of supply or energy
senses.definitionCN: 增加不同的供应或能源来源
senses.example: The grid diversified into wind and solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 电网向风能与太阳能多元化。
senses.why: Sources are supplies, so the same verb says: do not depend on one well, one pipe or one country.
senses.whyCN: 来源就是供应，所以同一个动词表达：不要只依赖一口井、一条管道或一个国家。

intro.en: Diversify is an English verb formed from Latin diversus 'turned apart' and facere 'to make'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: diversify 是英语动词，由拉丁语 diversus「转向别处」与 facere「制造」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn; its participle supplied the idea of being turned in another direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动；它的分词形式提供了「被转向另一方向」的意思。

items.en: Diversus meant turned apart or various, the direct ancestor of diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 意为被转开或多样的，是 diverse 与 diversity 的直接祖先。

items.en: Diversificare joined that adjective with facere 'to make' to mean to make different or varied.
items.cn: diversificare 把这个形容词与 facere「制造」结合，意为使不同、使多样。

items.en: French used the verb in ordinary speech, and English borrowed it in the seventeenth century as diversify.
items.cn: 法语在日常语言中使用这个动词，英语在十七世纪以 diversify 的形式借入。

items.en: Modern finance applied the verb to holdings and modern industry applied it to products, markets and regions.
items.cn: 现代金融把这个动词用于持有资产，现代产业则把它用于产品、市场与地区。

note.en: The first group is built on the same turning root and is often confused with it; the second group contains verbs of widening or varying.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「转」的词根上，常被混淆；第二组是表示扩大或变化的动词。

entries.definition: A change of route or an entertainment; it turns one thing away rather than adding kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改道或消遣；它把一样东西转开，而不是增加种类。

entries.definition: The state of being varied; it is the result, while diversify is the action that creates it.
entries.definitionCN: 多样的状态；它是结果，而 diversify 是创造它的动作。

entries.definition: Of many different kinds; it describes a set, not the process of changing it.
entries.definitionCN: 许多不同种类的；它描述一个集合，而不是改变它的过程。

entries.definition: To change the course of something; it does not mean to multiply its kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改变某物的方向；不表示增加其种类。

entries.definition: To make or become different over time; vary stresses change, diversify stresses adding kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 使或变得不同；vary 强调变化，diversify 强调增加种类。

entries.definition: To make wider in scope; it stresses extent rather than the number of kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 使范围更宽；强调广度而非种类的数量。

entries.definition: To grow in size or reach; expansion may stay within one business, while diversification must cross boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或范围上增长；扩张可以在同一业务内，而多元化必须跨界。

entries.definition: To distribute over an area; in finance it describes the physical result of diversifying.
entries.definitionCN: 分布到一片区域；在金融中描述分散化的实际结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The word is make plus turned apart: to diversify is to make things head in different directions.
normal.cn: 这个词是「制造」加「转向别处」：多元化就是让事物朝不同方向走。

normal.en: Money diversifies into assets, a firm into products, a region into industries, a farm into crops.
normal.cn: 资金分散到资产，企业扩展到产品，地区扩展到产业，农场扩展到作物。

normal.en: The fixed phrase diversify into marks the new field being entered.
normal.cn: 表示「扩展到某一领域」的固定说法标出正在进入的新领域。

normal.en: Diversify away from marks the old dependence being reduced.
normal.cn: 表示「从某一领域转向别处」的说法标出正在减少的旧依赖。

normal.en: The noun diversification and the adjective diversified come from this verb, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 名词 diversification 与形容词 diversified 都从这个动词而来，而不是反过来。

abstract.en: Picture one hand scattering the same seed over several fields, so no single storm can take the whole harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把同一种种子撒向好几块田，任何一场风暴都拿不走全部收成。

abstract.en: Picture a single stream split into several channels, each able to supply water if another dries.
abstract.cn: 想象一条水流分成几道渠，任何一条干了，其余仍能供水。

abstract.en: Picture a person's work splitting into several skills, so one closed door does not end the career.
