sceneCN: 这里 stomatal 是「气孔关闭的」（第 5 个义项：由气孔限制水汽散失）；句意：关闭气孔是抵御干旱的第一道防线。

pos.zh: 气孔的；与气孔有关的
由气孔引起的；气孔性的

forms.label: 比较级（更受气孔影响的）
最高级（最受气孔影响的）

senses.title: Of the openings
senses.definition: relating to the openings on a leaf surface
senses.definitionCN: 与叶片表面的气孔有关的
senses.example: Stomatal structure differs between sun and shade leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 阳叶与阴叶的气孔结构不同。
senses.why: The suffix -al simply attaches the noun to another noun: structure, anatomy, question.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 只是把名词挂到另一个名词上：结构、解剖、问题。

senses.title: Movement
senses.titleCN: 运动的：孔口开合的动作
senses.definition: relating to the opening and closing of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔孔口开合有关的
senses.example: Stomatal movement follows the light and the water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔运动随光照与供水而变。
senses.why: The pores move, and the adjective labels the study of that movement rather than the pore itself.
senses.whyCN: 这些孔会动，形容词标的是对这种动作的研究，而不是孔本身。

senses.title: Conductance
senses.definition: relating to the conductance of water vapour and gases through the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与水汽和气体经气孔传导有关的
senses.example: Stomatal conductance fell by half at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午气孔导度降了一半。
senses.why: Physiologists treat the pores as a resistor, and the adjective names the value of that resistance.
senses.whyCN: 生理学家把这些孔当成一个阻力，形容词命名的是那个阻力的值。

senses.title: Density
senses.titleCN: 密度的：单位叶面有多少孔
senses.definition: relating to the number of pores per unit area
senses.definitionCN: 与单位面积气孔数目有关的
senses.example: Stomatal density is a common measure in paleobotany.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔密度是古植物学常用的指标。
senses.why: Counting the pores per area makes them a trait, and the adjective marks that trait.
senses.whyCN: 按面积数孔让它们成为一种性状，形容词标出这一性状。

senses.title: Closure
senses.definition: relating to the closing of the pores, especially under stress
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔关闭（尤指受胁迫时）有关的
senses.example: Stomatal closure is the first defence against drought.
senses.exampleCN: 关闭气孔是抵御干旱的第一道防线。
senses.why: Closing is the active choice of the plant, so the adjective often appears with closure and stress.
senses.whyCN: 关闭是植物主动的选择，所以这个形容词常与关闭和胁迫连用。

senses.title: Limitation
senses.titleCN: 限制的：光合被气孔卡住
senses.definition: relating to the limit that the pores put on photosynthesis
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔对光合作用造成的限制有关的
senses.example: Stomatal limitation explains the midday dip in carbon uptake.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔限制解释了正午碳吸收的下陷。
senses.why: When the pores shut, carbon cannot enter, and the adjective names that bottleneck.
senses.whyCN: 孔一关，碳进不来，形容词命名的是这个瓶颈。

senses.title: Regulation
senses.titleCN: 调节的：植物对孔口的控制
senses.definition: relating to the plant's regulation of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与植物对气孔的调控有关的
senses.example: Stomatal regulation keeps water loss within limits.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔调节把失水控制在限度之内。
senses.why: The adjective marks control rather than structure: who decides when the valve moves.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标的是控制而不是结构：谁决定阀门何时动。

senses.title: Distribution
senses.titleCN: 分布的：上下表面的差别
senses.definition: relating to where the pores are placed on the leaf
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔在叶面上的位置分布有关的
senses.example: Stomatal distribution differs between the two surfaces.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔在两个表面上的分布不同。
senses.why: Placement is a separate fact from number, and the adjective covers it.
senses.whyCN: 位置与数目是两件事，形容词也覆盖了位置。

senses.title: Evolutionary
senses.titleCN: 演化的：气孔在植物史上的出现
senses.definition: relating to the evolutionary origin and change of the pores
senses.definitionCN: 与气孔在演化上的起源与变化有关的
senses.example: Stomatal evolution tracks the rise of land plants.
senses.exampleCN: 气孔的演化与陆生植物的兴起同步。
senses.why: The trait has a history, and geology uses the adjective for changes over millions of years.
senses.whyCN: 这一性状有历史，地质学用这个形容词指数百万年尺度的变化。

intro.en: Stomatal is the adjective of stomata, made with the Latin-derived suffix -al on a Greek noun.
intro.cn: stomatal 是 stomata 的形容词，在希腊名词上加了拉丁来源的后缀 -al。

items.en: Greek stoma 'mouth' is the base; the plural stomata entered botany in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 希腊 stoma「口」是基础词；复数 stomata 于十九世纪进入植物学。

items.en: The suffix -al, from Latin -alis, means 'relating to' and is added to nouns of any origin.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 来自拉丁 -alis，意为「与……有关的」，可加在任何来源的名词上。

items.en: Plant anatomists needed an adjective for pore structure, movement and density, and stomatal supplied all three.
items.cn: 植物解剖学家需要一个形容词来指孔的结构、运动与密度，stomatal 一次满足了这三样。

items.en: Twentieth-century physiology fixed phrases such as stomatal conductance and stomatal limitation.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生理学固定了 stomatal conductance、stomatal limitation 这类短语。

items.en: The same adjective now appears in studies that read ancient carbon dioxide from fossil pore counts.
items.cn: 同一个形容词现在也出现在从化石孔数读出古代二氧化碳的研究里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the elements are certain, but the first printed use of the adjective is undated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：成分确定，但这个形容词首次印刷使用的年份没有记载。

note.en: Group one separates the noun family from look-alikes; group two holds adjectives for nearby leaf surfaces and openings.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词词族与形近词；第二组列出描述邻近叶面与开口的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural noun itself; the adjective adds -al and shifts the final syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 复数名词本身；形容词加 -al，并把末音节改掉。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning 'having pores'; stomatal is the usual modern form for 'relating to pores'.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的形容词，意为「有孔的」；现代常用 stomatal 表示「与孔有关的」。

entries.definition: The organ, from the same Greek word for 'mouth'; the meaning is medical, not botanical.
entries.definitionCN: 器官，来自同一个希腊词「口」；意义属医学，不属植物学。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the mouth; the suffix -itis marks disease.
entries.definitionCN: 口腔炎症；后缀 -itis 标出疾病。

entries.definition: Relating to the outer cell layer that carries the pores.
entries.definitionCN: 与承载气孔的外层细胞有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to the waxy covering that limits water loss around the pores.
entries.definitionCN: 与气孔周围限制失水的蜡质层有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to the pores in bark, the woody counterpart of leaf pores.
entries.definitionCN: 与树皮上的孔有关，是叶孔在木质部分的对应物。

entries.definition: Relating to pores that release liquid water rather than vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 与释放液态水而非水汽的孔有关的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实后缀与真实搭配，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: stomata + -al: 'relating to the leaf's small mouths'.
normal.cn: stomata 加 -al：「与叶片小嘴有关的」。

normal.en: The family: stoma, stomata, stomatous, stomatitis.
normal.cn: 同族：stoma、stomata、stomatous、stomatitis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: stomatal closure, stomatal conductance, stomatal density.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：气孔关闭、气孔导度、气孔密度。

normal.en: Three questions the adjective answers: how many, how open, how much flows.
normal.cn: 这个形容词回答三个问题：有多少、开多大、通过多少。

normal.en: Closure, limitation and regulation are the stress words that go with it.
normal.cn: 关闭、限制、调节是常与它连用的胁迫词。

abstract.en: Picture a valve chart on the wall of a greenhouse, with every valve drawn small.
abstract.cn: 想象温室墙上挂着一张阀门图，每个阀门都画得很小。

abstract.en: Picture a plant choosing to shut its windows rather than lose its water.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物选择关上窗户，而不是失水。

abstract.en: Picture a number written on a leaf that says how tightly the leaf is holding its breath.
abstract.cn: 想象叶片上写着一个数，说明它屏气屏得多紧。

examples.en: Stomatal closure is the first defence against drought.
examples.cn: 关闭气孔是抵御干旱的第一道防线。

examples.en: Stomatal conductance fell by half at noon.
examples.cn: 正午气孔导度降了一半。

examples.en: Stomatal density is a common measure in paleobotany.
examples.cn: 气孔密度是古植物学常用的指标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「气孔（stomata）＋的（-al）」——凡指叶面小孔的数目、开合与导度

root: 希腊 stoma「口」的复数 stomata 加拉丁来源的形容词后缀 -al（来自 -alis，「与……有关的」）。词根清晰，形容词首见年代无确切记载。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all point at the same pores from different angles: structure, movement, conductance, density, closure, limitation, regulation, placement, and evolutionary history.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从不同角度指向同一批小孔：结构、运动、导度、密度、关闭、限制、调节、位置，以及演化史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every statement about a leaf's small valves, whether of size, number or state.
core.cn: 核心意象：关于叶片那些小阀门的一切陈述，无论讲大小、数目还是状态。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTE: the adjective first just says 'of the pores'.
branches.cn: 属性：这个形容词最初只说「与孔有关的」。

branches.en: CONTROL: movement and regulation describe what the plant decides.
branches.cn: 控制：运动与调节描述植物所作的决定。

branches.en: FLOW: conductance measures it, limitation names where it blocks.
branches.cn: 流动：导度测量它，限制命名它卡住的地方。

branches.en: COUNT AND PLACE: how many per area, and where they sit.
branches.cn: 数目与位置：单位面积多少，以及它们待在哪。

branches.en: STRESS AND TIME: closure under drought, evolution over ages.
branches.cn: 胁迫与时间：干旱下关闭，漫长年代里的演化。

intro.en: Stomatal is a Greek noun plus the Latin-derived suffix -al; the suffix is Latin, the base is Greek.
intro.cn: stomatal 是希腊名词加拉丁来源的后缀 -al；后缀属拉丁，基础词属希腊。

latinIntro.en: Greek stoma 'mouth' supplies the base; Latin -alis supplies the adjective ending; the combination is modern scientific English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 stoma「口」提供基础；拉丁 -alis 提供形容词词尾；组合发生在现代科学英语里。

items.example: It attaches to nouns of any origin.
items.exampleCN: 它可加在任何来源的名词上。

items.example: An older synonym of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 该形容词较早的同义词。

items.example: The medical branch of the family.

definition_zh: 关于、就……而言；在……方面（正式用语，引出论述或处理的对象）
definition_en: concerning; in connection with a particular subject or matter
core_image: 一束目光落在文件上某一栏，其余部分暂被搁在一旁
scene: 会议开到最后，主持人把散落的议题逐项归位，先点出需要表决的那一条。 With regard to the budget, the committee asked for a second review.
sceneCN: 这里取「关于、就……而言」（第 1 个义项：正式引出论述对象）；句意为关于预算，委员会要求再审议一次。

pos.zh: 介词短语：关于；就……而言

senses.title: A formal topic marker
senses.titleCN: 话题义：正式引出论述对象
senses.definition: used at the start of a statement to name the matter that the statement deals with
senses.definitionCN: 用在陈述开头，点出该陈述所要处理的事项
senses.example: With regard to the schedule, no change has been made.
senses.exampleCN: 关于日程，目前没有任何变动。
senses.why: Regard began as a look, and looking at a matter is the first step in discussing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指注视，把目光落到一件事上，正是讨论它的第一步。

senses.title: The letter and the memo
senses.titleCN: 公文义：书信与备忘录用语
senses.definition: in correspondence it opens a paragraph that answers or raises one specific point
senses.definitionCN: 在书信往来中，用于开启答复或提出某一具体问题的段落
senses.example: With regard to your enquiry of the fifth, we reply as follows.
senses.exampleCN: 关于您五日来函的询问，我方答复如下。
senses.why: Written office language needs a dignified opener, and this phrase supplies one without bluntness.
senses.whyCN: 书面办公语言需要得体的起句，这个短语提供了不生硬的起句。

senses.title: Unlike the participle
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：与现在分词形式不同
senses.definition: the phrase is a prepositional frame, while the participial form works as a preposition on its own
senses.definitionCN: 这个短语是介词框架，而与之形近的分词形式本身就是一个介词
senses.example: With regard to the invoice, please see the attached note.
senses.exampleCN: 关于发票，请见所附说明。
senses.why: A frame needs its noun after of, whereas the single participle takes its object directly.
senses.whyCN: 框架要在介词后接名词，而单个分词直接带宾语。

senses.title: Register beside as regards
senses.titleCN: 语域义：与另一变体的分工
senses.definition: the frame is neutral formal, while the shorter variant sounds older and more legal
senses.definitionCN: 这个框架属中性正式，较短的变体显得更古旧、更偏法律
senses.example: With regard to staffing, the board will decide in June.
senses.exampleCN: 关于人员配置，董事会将在六月决定。
senses.why: Both forms say the same thing, but one is plainly modern and the other carries a legal flavour.
senses.whyCN: 两种形式意思相同，但一种明显现代，另一种带法律气味。

senses.title: The in-regard variant
senses.titleCN: 变体义：介词换成另一介词的近义形式
senses.definition: a variant with a different preposition carries the same topic-marking function in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 换用另一个介词的变体，在正式文字中承担同样的话题标记功能
senses.example: With regard to the lease, the tenant raised three points.
senses.exampleCN: 关于租约，租户提出了三点意见。
senses.why: Preposition choice here is a matter of idiom rather than meaning, so the two variants can replace each other.
senses.whyCN: 这里介词的选择是习惯问题而非意义问题，因此两个变体可以互换。

senses.title: A stance on a matter
senses.definition: it can introduce the matter about which a person or body expresses an opinion or a concern
senses.definitionCN: 可引出某人或某机构表达意见、关切所针对的事项
senses.example: The ministry was cautious with regard to the findings.
senses.exampleCN: 该部对这些发现持谨慎态度。
senses.why: Once a matter is looked at, a judgement may follow, and the phrase can carry that stance as well.
senses.whyCN: 一件事被注视之后可能引出判断，这个短语也能承载那种态度。

senses.title: Scope of a rule
senses.titleCN: 适用范围义：条款所针对的对象
senses.definition: in regulations it identifies the persons or goods that a provision applies to
senses.definitionCN: 在规章中，指出某项条款所适用的对象或货物
senses.example: With regard to imported goods, the tariff applies from July.
senses.exampleCN: 关于进口货物，该关税自七月起适用。
senses.why: A rule must say what it looks at, and the phrase marks exactly that scope.
senses.whyCN: 规则必须说明它看向什么，这个短语标的正是那个范围。

senses.title: Not the sense of esteem
senses.definition: although the noun can mean esteem, the phrase marks a topic and carries no flattery
senses.definitionCN: 尽管这个名词可表尊敬，短语只标话题，不含恭维之意
senses.example: With regard to the witness, the phrase shows a topic, not respect.
senses.exampleCN: 就证人一词而言，这个短语标的是话题，不是敬意。
senses.why: The esteem sense lives in other patterns, and mixing the two produces a unintended compliment.
senses.whyCN: 尊敬义活在其他句式中，两者混用会意外变成恭维。

intro.en: Regard comes from Old French regarder, to look at, formed with the Latin prefix re- and a Germanic stem meaning to guard or watch. The Latin prefix is secure; the stem is reconstructed.
intro.cn: regard 来自古法语 regarder「注视」，由拉丁语前缀 re- 与表看守的日耳曼语词干构成。拉丁语前缀清楚；词干为重构形式。

items.en: The stem behind the French verb meant to watch or guard and is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 法语动词背后的词干意为看守、警戒，属重构形式而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The Latin prefix added a sense of back or again, so the verb pictured a repeated look.
items.cn: 拉丁语前缀加上回、再的意思，因此动词描绘的是一再投去的目光。

items.en: The French verb meant to look at or to heed, and the noun named a look or attention.
items.cn: 法语动词意为注视、留意，其名词指目光或注意。

items.en: Attention to a person's worth produced the sense of esteem, which is why the plural can mean greetings.
items.cn: 对人价值的关注产生尊敬义，因此复数形式可指问候。

items.en: The topic frame belongs to modern official and academic prose; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个话题框架属于近代公文与学术文字，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group marks a topic in a different form; the second group are plain prepositions of subject matter.
note.cn: 第一组以不同形式标出话题；第二组是朴素的关涉介词。

entries.definition: The participle works alone and takes its object directly.
entries.definitionCN: 分词单独作介词，直接带宾语。

entries.definition: The variant sounds dated and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 这个变体显得古旧而正式。

entries.definition: A different preposition carries the same topic function.
entries.definitionCN: 换一个介词，承担同样的话题功能。

entries.definition: It links two matters rather than merely naming one topic.
entries.definitionCN: 它连接两件事，而不只是点出一个话题。

entries.definition: A single word with the same formal subject marker.
entries.definitionCN: 单个词，同样正式地点出主题。

entries.definition: The ordinary spoken equivalent with no official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语的对应说法，没有公文语气。

entries.definition: It introduces a matter under discussion, often after a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 引出讨论中的事项，常置于动词后。

entries.definition: A bare preposition for the subject of a book or a talk.
entries.definitionCN: 单个介词，指书或谈话的主题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real look-root, the Germanic guard stem, the later esteem sense and the real preposition frame.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的注视词根、日耳曼语看守词干、后来的尊敬义，以及真实的介词框架。

normal.en: To regard is to look, so the phrase first directs the reader's eyes to one matter.
normal.cn: 看待就是看，因此这个短语先把读者的目光引到一件事上。

normal.en: A look can harden into esteem, but the topic frame carries no praise.
normal.cn: 注视会沉淀为尊敬，但话题框架不含褒扬。

normal.en: One frame takes a noun after of; the participle takes its object alone.
normal.cn: 一个框架在介词后接名词；分词则直接带宾语。

normal.en: The shorter variants are older and more legal in flavour.
normal.cn: 较短的变体更古旧，法律气味更重。

normal.en: Regulations use it to state what a provision applies to.
normal.cn: 规章用它说明条款适用于什么。

abstract.en: Like a spotlight aimed at one column of a page while the rest stays dim.
abstract.cn: 像一束光打在一页纸的某一栏，其余部分仍暗着。

abstract.en: Like a bookmark placed at a chapter: it says where to read, not what to think.
abstract.cn: 像夹在某一章的书签：说明读哪里，不说怎么想。

abstract.en: Like a clerk turning a file so the relevant page faces the reader.
abstract.cn: 像职员把卷宗转到相关那一页朝向读者。

examples.en: With regard to your question, the answer is in the appendix.
examples.cn: 关于您的问题，答案在附录里。

examples.en: No decision has been taken with regard to the site.
examples.cn: 关于选址尚未作出决定。

examples.en: With regard to cost, the two plans are close.
examples.cn: 就成本而言，两个方案相近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「威兹 瑞嘎德 图」——目光只落在文件的一栏：关于、就……而言

root: 核心名词意为关注，来自古法语 regarder「注视」，由拉丁语前缀 re- 与日耳曼语系表看守的词干构成，后者为重构形式；该短语为近代公文定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the formal topic marker, correspondence openings, the grammatical boundary against the participle, register beside the older variant, the preposition variant, a stated stance, the scope of a rule and the exclusion of the esteem sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项涵盖：正式话题标记、书信起句、与分词形式的语法边界、与古旧变体的语域分工、介词变体、表态、条款适用范围，以及排除尊敬义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of attention falling on one column of a document while the rest stays in shadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束注意力落在文件的一栏上，其余部分留在阴影里。

branches.en: THE TOPIC: one matter is singled out for the reader, whatever preposition is chosen.
branches.cn: 话题：无论选哪个介词，都是把一件事单独提给读者。

branches.en: THE LETTER: office correspondence needs a dignified opening for a single point.
branches.cn: 书信：公文往来需要得体的起句来引出单一问题。

branches.en: THE FORM AND THE TONE: a frame differs from a participle, and one variant sounds older.
branches.cn: 形式与语气：框架不同于分词，一个变体也更古旧。

branches.en: THE STANCE: a body may look at a finding and then say how it views it.
branches.cn: 立场：机构先看向某项发现，再表明如何看待它。

branches.en: THE SCOPE AND THE LIMIT: rules say what they cover, and no esteem is implied.
branches.cn: 范围与边界：规则说明覆盖什么，且不含敬意。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin prefix and a Germanic stem inside a French verb, then adds a modern topic frame.
intro.cn: 这个短语的动词在法语中由拉丁语前缀与日耳曼语词干合成，后来又加上近代话题框架。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin element is the prefix re-, meaning back or again; the stem that means guard is Germanic and reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 其中唯一的拉丁成分是前缀 re-，意为回、再；表看守的词干属日耳曼语，为重构形式。

items.example: The prefix adds a repeated or returned action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上重复或返回的动作。

items.example: English keeps both the look and the heed.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼留注视与留意两义。

items.example: The participle became a preposition in its own right.
The suffix removes the looking entirely.
The negative prefix reverses the attention.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把注意力反转。

items.example: The plural turns attention into a courtesy.
A variant preposition marks the same topic.
items.exampleCN: 换一个介词标出同一话题。

items.example: The older variant survives in legal prose.
items.exampleCN: 较古旧的变体留在法律文字里。

items.example: The frame is standard in official writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在公文中是标准用法。

definition_zh: 范式；典范；样板；（语言学）词形变化表；（科学哲学）理论框架
definition_en: a model or pattern; in grammar, the full set of forms a word can take; in science, the shared assumptions within which research is done
core_image: 一块竖起的样板，旁边整齐排着同一套变化的所有形态
scene: 语言学课堂上，黑板上画着一整张动词变位表。 The teacher tapped the whole paradigm with her pointer and said that every cell showed one form of the same verb.
sceneCN: 这里 paradigm 是「词形变化表」（第 1 个义项：所有形态并排展示）；句意：老师用教鞭敲着整张词形变化表，说每一格都是同一个动词的一种形式。图中可辨识物件：黑板、变位表格、粉笔、教鞭、讲台。

pos.zh: 范式；典范；样板
（语言学）词形变化表；词形变化系统
（科学哲学）范式；理论框架

collocations.zh: 范式转移；思维框架的根本转变

derivatives.zh: 范式的；典范的；词形变化上的
以范式的方式；作为典范地

senses.title: The grammar table: all forms side by side
senses.titleCN: 语法表：所有形态并排展示
senses.definition: in grammar, a table showing all the inflected forms of a word, such as a verb's persons and tenses
senses.definitionCN: 语法中展示一个词全部屈折形式的表格，如动词的人称与时态
senses.example: The students copied the paradigm of the verb into their notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把那个动词的变位表抄进笔记本。
senses.why: Greek paradeigma meant a pattern shown beside something. A grammar table does exactly that: it sets every form of one word next to the others so the pattern becomes visible at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 paradeigma 意为“摆在旁边给人看的样板”。语法表正是如此：把一个词的所有形态并排摆开，让模式一眼可见。

senses.title: The inflectional system behind the table
senses.titleCN: 表格背后的词形变化系统
senses.definition: the whole system of inflections that a class of words follows
senses.definitionCN: 某一类词所遵循的整套屈折变化系统
senses.example: English nouns have a much simpler paradigm than Latin nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 英语名词的变格系统比拉丁语名词简单得多。
senses.why: Once the table is learned, the table stands for the rule. Linguists speak of the paradigm as the system, not the paper, because the same pattern can be reproduced for any word of the class.
senses.whyCN: 表格一旦被掌握，表就代表了规则。语言学家说的 paradigm 是系统而不是那张纸，因为同一模式可以为该类词中的任何一词重现。

senses.title: A model worth copying
senses.definition: a model, example, or pattern that others are expected to follow
senses.definitionCN: 供他人效仿的模范、例子或模式
senses.example: Her career became a paradigm for young scientists.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职业生涯成了年轻科学家的样板。
senses.why: The Greek word already carried the sense of an example set before a learner. The table is a pattern to copy, so the word naturally extends from grammar to any model held up for imitation.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词本就带有“摆在学习者面前的例子”之义。表格是可以照抄的模式，因此这个词自然从语法扩展到任何被举起来供人效仿的样板。

senses.title: Kuhn's scientific paradigm
senses.definition: in the philosophy of science, the set of shared assumptions, methods, and exemplars within which a scientific community works
senses.definitionCN: 科学哲学中，一个科学共同体工作其间的共同假设、方法与范例的总和
senses.example: Newtonian mechanics was the ruling paradigm for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿力学在两个世纪里是占统治地位的范式。
senses.why: Thomas Kuhn adopted the word in 1962 because a scientific community, like a language class, works from a shared set of exemplary solutions. The pattern is not written on a table but held in common, and that is what makes normal research possible.
senses.whyCN: 托马斯·库恩在 1962 年采用这个词，因为科学共同体就像一个语言班级，依靠一套共同的范例解法工作。这个模式不写在表上，而是被共同持有，正是它让常规研究成为可能。

senses.title: The framework of an era
senses.definition: the dominant set of ideas and assumptions of a period or field, which makes some questions askable and others invisible
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期或领域占主导的观念与假设集合，它决定哪些问题可被提出、哪些则不可见
senses.example: The paradigm of endless growth shaped city planning for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 无限增长的范式塑造了城市规划数十年。
senses.why: A shared framework does more than guide work: it decides what counts as a problem. That is why the word can name the invisible boundary of an age, not just a method inside it.
senses.whyCN: 共同的框架不只是指导工作：它决定什么才算“问题”。因此这个词可以命名一个时代的无形边界，而不只是时代内部的一种方法。

senses.title: A business or technological paradigm
senses.definition: the established way an industry produces value, especially before a disruptive change
senses.definitionCN: 一个行业创造价值的既定方式，尤指在颠覆性变化之前
senses.example: Subscription pricing became the new paradigm for software.
senses.exampleCN: 订阅制定价成了软件业的新范式。
senses.why: Business borrows the scientific word for the same reason: a whole industry can share one model of how money is made. A shift in that model rearranges winners and losers, not just methods.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用这个科学词，理由相同：整个行业可以共用一个“钱如何赚”的模式。模式一变，赢家与输家就会重排，而不只是方法更换。

senses.title: A programming paradigm
senses.definition: a fundamental style of programming, such as object-oriented or functional programming, that shapes how problems are expressed
senses.definitionCN: 编程的根本风格，如面向对象或函数式编程，它决定问题如何被表达
senses.example: The course moves from procedural to object-oriented paradigms.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从过程式范式过渡到面向对象范式。
senses.why: A programming style is a grammar of solutions: it tells you what a problem looks like before you solve it. The word fits because the style is learned as a pattern and then applied to new cases.
senses.whyCN: 编程风格是一套“解法的语法”：它在解题之前就规定问题长什么样。这个词之所以适用，是因为这种风格作为模式被学会，再套用到新个例上。

senses.title: The paradigm case in philosophy
senses.definition: an example that is taken as the clearest instance of a concept and against which other cases are judged
senses.definitionCN: 被当作某概念最清晰实例、并用来衡量其他个案的例子
senses.example: A clear case of knowledge serves as the paradigm case in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 一个清晰的知识实例成为这场争论中的典型个案。
senses.why: Here the model is a single case rather than a table. Philosophy needs one uncontested instance to anchor a concept, and that instance is held up beside doubtful cases exactly as the Greek word suggests.
senses.whyCN: 这里作为样板的是单个案例而不是表格。哲学需要一个无争议的实例来锚定概念，这个实例被摆到可疑案例旁边，正是希腊词字面上的做法。

intro.en: Paradigm is Greek in origin and reached English through Late Latin. Its parts are well attested; the modern scientific sense is a deliberate twentieth-century borrowing.
intro.cn: paradigm 源自希腊语，经晚期拉丁语进入英语。其构词成分有明确记载；现代科学义是 20 世纪有意的借用。

items.en: Paradigm is recorded in English meaning 'an example, a model'. It comes from Late Latin paradigma, from Greek paradeigma 'pattern, model, sample'.
items.cn: paradigm 于 15 世纪晚期进入英语，意为“例子、模范”。它来自晚期拉丁语 paradigma，再上溯希腊语 paradeigma“模式、样板、样本”。

items.en: Paradeigma is formed from para- 'beside' and the verb deiknynai 'to show, point out'. The literal picture is something shown beside something else so that it can be compared.
items.cn: paradeigma 由 para-“在旁边”与动词 deiknynai“展示、指出来”构成。字面画面是把某物摆在另一物旁边，以便比较。

items.en: Deiknynai goes back to PIE *deik- 'to show, point out', the same family as English token and the deictic words that point at things. The asterisk marks a reconstructed root.
items.cn: deiknynai 上溯原始印欧语 *deik-“展示、指出”，与英语 token 以及表示“指指点点”的指示词同族。星号表示这是重构词根。

items.en: The grammatical sense is recorded: a paradigm is the table of all the inflected forms of a word. The table is the model shown beside the word it describes.
items.cn: 语法义记录于 16 世纪后期：paradigm 是一个词全部屈折形式的表格。表格就是摆在所描述之词旁边的样板。

items.en: Thomas Kuhn's The Structure of Scientific Revolutions makes paradigm a name for a scientific community's shared framework. Kuhn later said he preferred 'disciplinary matrix', but the popular sense stuck.
items.cn: 托马斯·库恩《科学革命的结构》使 paradigm 成为“科学共同体共享框架”的名称。库恩后来说他更愿意用 disciplinary matrix，但流行开来的仍是 paradigm。

note.en: The first group is a para- family that is easy to confuse; the second compares words for models and frameworks.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的 para- 词族；第二组比较表示“样板与框架”的词。

entries.definition: a distinct section of writing. Its para- means beside, and the second part is graphein 'to write', not deiknynai.
entries.definitionCN: 文章中的一个独立段落。它的 para- 是“在旁边”，后半是 graphein“写”，不是 deiknynai。

entries.definition: a statement that seems to contradict itself. Its second part is doxa 'opinion', so it is 'beside opinion', not 'shown beside'.
entries.definitionCN: 看似自相矛盾的说法。后半是 doxa“意见”，所以是“与意见相悖”，不是“摆在旁边展示”。

entries.definition: loss of movement in the body. Its para- means beside or beyond, and lysis means loosening, a medical compound far from paradigm.
entries.definitionCN: 身体失去运动能力。它的 para- 是“在旁边、超出”，lysis 是“松开”，这一医学复合词与 paradigm 相距很远。

entries.definition: a person trained to give emergency medical care alongside doctors. The para- means alongside, and the second part is medical.
entries.definitionCN: 与医生并肩提供急救护理的人。para- 是“并肩”，后半是 medical。

entries.definition: a simplified representation or an example to follow. It is the broad everyday word; paradigm adds the idea of a whole framework shared by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 简化的表征，或可供效仿的榜样。它是最宽泛的日常词；paradigm 增加了“一个群体共享的整套框架”之意。

entries.definition: the supporting structure or set of ideas that holds something together. It stresses structure, while paradigm stresses the exemplary pattern inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑结构，或把事物组织起来的一套观念。它强调结构，而 paradigm 强调结构内部的典范模式。

entries.definition: the original model from which copies are made, often in psychology or literature. It is more about an original than about a working community.
entries.definitionCN: 被复制所依据的原型，常用于心理学或文学。它更强调“原初”，而不是一个工作共同体。

entries.definition: a shaped pattern used to produce identical copies. It is concrete and often physical, while paradigm is usually conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制作相同副本的样板。它具体、常为实物，而 paradigm 通常是概念性的。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sound and the grammar table, then three abstract images about shared frameworks.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕读音与语法表的挂钩，再用三个关于“共享框架”的抽象画面。

normal.en: para- means beside, and -digm comes from showing: a paradigm is a sample shown beside the thing it explains.
normal.cn: para- 是“在旁边”，-digm 来自“展示”：paradigm 就是摆在被解释之物旁边的样本。

normal.en: Think of a Latin verb chart: amo, amas, amat down the page. That chart is a paradigm, and every form is a cell in it.
normal.cn: 想一张拉丁语动词表：amo、amas、amat 一路排下去。那张表就是 paradigm，每个形态是表里的一格。

normal.en: A paradigm shift is not a new answer to the old question; it is a new table on which the questions are written.
normal.cn: paradigm shift 不是给旧问题换新答案，而是换了一张写问题的表。

normal.en: Say it PARA-dime, not para-DIG-em: the stress is on the first syllable, like the pattern standing in front.
normal.cn: 读作 PARA-dime，而不是 para-DIG-em：重音在第一音节，就像样板立在最前面。

normal.en: Grammar first, science later: the word spent four centuries as a schoolroom table before Kuhn made it a theory of science.
normal.cn: 先有语法，后有科学：这个词在教室里当了几百年的变位表，之后库恩才把它变成科学理论。

abstract.en: A paradigm is a frame you cannot see while you are inside it. You notice it only when another frame appears beside it.
abstract.cn: 范式是你身处其中时看不见的框。只有当另一个框出现在旁边，你才注意到它。

abstract.en: Paradigms save thought by pre-deciding what a problem looks like; that saving is also their danger.
abstract.cn: 范式通过事先决定“问题长什么样”来节省思考；这种节省也正是它的危险。

abstract.en: Every paradigm is a table with missing cells: what a community never writes down is part of the pattern too.
abstract.cn: 每个范式都是一张有空格子的表：一个共同体从不写下的东西，也是模式的一部分。

examples.en: The textbook prints the paradigm of the noun at the top of each chapter.
examples.cn: 教科书在每章开头印出该名词的变格表。

examples.en: Kuhn argued that a paradigm shift is a change of the questions a field can ask.
examples.cn: 库恩认为，范式转移是一个领域“能问什么问题”的改变。

examples.en: Object-oriented programming is a paradigm, not a language.
examples.cn: 面向对象编程是一种范式，而不是一门语言。

dict_mnemonic.note: para- 记成“在旁边”，-digm 记成“展示”：把一整套样板摆在旁边给你照着做，就是范式。
dict_mnemonic.text: para（在旁边）+ deiknynai（展示）→ 摆在旁边的样板 → 词形表、典范、科学范式

root: 希腊 paradeigma“样板”，来自 para-（在旁边）+ deiknynai（展示，原始印欧语 *deik-）→ 晚期拉丁 paradigma → 英语 paradigm。

sensesIntro.en: The senses begin with a grammar table that shows every form of one word, move to the system behind that table, then to any model held up for copying, and finally to the large shared frameworks of science, an era, an industry, a programming style, and a single exemplary case.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从一张展示单词全部形态的语法表开始，转到表格背后的系统，再到任何被举起来供人照做的样板，最后扩展到科学、时代、行业、编程风格乃至单个典型个案这些大型共享框架。

core.en: A pattern set beside the thing it explains, so that every form can be seen at once
core.cn: 摆在被解释之物旁边的样板，让所有形态一次看全

branches.en: The table and the rule: a printed chart of forms, and the inflectional system it displays.
branches.cn: 表与规则：印着形态的表格，以及它所展示的屈折系统。

branches.en: A model worth copying: an example held up for others to follow.
branches.cn: 值得照做的样板：被举出来让别人跟随的例子。

branches.en: Shared assumptions: a scientific community's framework, and the invisible boundary of an era.
branches.cn: 共享假设：科学共同体的框架，以及一个时代的无形边界。

branches.en: Working styles: how an industry makes money, and how a programmer expresses a problem.
branches.cn: 工作风格：一个行业如何赚钱，以及程序员如何表达问题。

branches.en: The typical case: the clearest instance of a concept, used to judge other cases.
branches.cn: 典型个案：某概念最清晰的实例，用来衡量其他个案。

intro.en: Paradigm is a compound of two Greek parts, and its family is mostly Greek-derived: the adjective, the adverb, the shift, the case, and the verb of making something a pattern.
intro.cn: paradigm 由两个希腊成分构成，其词族多为希腊来源：形容词、副词、转移、个案，以及“使成范式”的动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin route is paradigma, a Late Latin borrowing of Greek paradeigma. Latin adds no new root; it only carries the Greek compound into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语环节是 paradigma，即晚期拉丁语对希腊语 paradeigma 的借用。拉丁语没有增加新词根，只是把这个希腊复合词送进法语和英语。

items.meaning: a pattern or model; a table of forms; a shared framework
items.meaningCN: 样板或模式；形态表；共享框架
items.example: The discovery broke the old paradigm.
items.exampleCN: 这一发现打破了旧范式。

items.meaning: serving as a model; relating to a paradigm or to inflection
items.meaningCN: 典范性的；与范式或词形变化有关的
items.example: Her response was paradigmatic of the school's method.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答是该学派方法的典型代表。

items.meaning: in a way that exemplifies a pattern
items.meaningCN: 以典范的方式；作为模式地
items.example: The case is paradigmatically a case of trust.
items.exampleCN: 这个案例在范式意义上正是一个信任案例。

items.meaning: a fundamental change in the shared framework of a field
items.meaningCN: 一个领域共享框架的根本改变
items.example: The internet caused a paradigm shift in retail.
items.exampleCN: 互联网引发了零售业的范式转移。

items.meaning: the clearest instance used to anchor a concept
items.meaningCN: 用来锚定概念的最清晰实例
items.example: The paradigm case shapes how other cases are judged.
items.exampleCN: 典型个案决定了其他案例如何被评判。

items.meaning: to treat or present something as a model
items.meaningCN: 把某物当作范式来处理或呈现
items.example: The textbook paradigmatizes one method above the rest.
items.exampleCN: 这本教科书把一种方法树为高于其余的范式。

items.example: Deiknynai is the second half of paradeigma.
items.exampleCN: deiknynai 是 paradeigma 的后半部分。

items.meaning: pointing, as in words like this and here
items.meaningCN: 指示性的，如 this、here 这类词
items.example: This and here are deictic words.
items.exampleCN: this 和 here 都是指示词。

latinEntries.structure: Greek paradeigma borrowed into Late Latin
latinEntries.example: Late Latin paradigma passed into Old French and English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁语 paradigma 传入古法语与英语。

latinEntries.example: The Late Latin adjective underlies English paradigmatic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这一晚期拉丁语形容词是英语 paradigmatic 的基础。

definition_zh: 恋情；（尤指秘密的）风流韵事
definition_en: a love affair, especially a secret or illicit one
core_image: 深夜递出的一封信：藏在披风下的恋情
scene: 宫廷里人人低声议论着王妃与乐师的传闻。 The queen's secret amour was the talk of the entire court.
sceneCN: 这里的 amour 是「秘密恋情」（第 1 个义项：隐秘的恋爱关系）；句意是王后的秘密恋情成为整个宫廷的谈资。

pos.zh: 恋情；风流韵事

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「含情脉脉的；多情的」
amorous 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「多情；柔情」
同根词，义为「情人；尤指不正当的恋人」

senses.title: A secret or illicit love affair
senses.titleCN: 秘密恋情：隐秘或越界的恋爱关系
senses.definition: a romantic relationship kept hidden, often because it is improper
senses.definitionCN: 因不合礼俗而隐藏的恋爱关系
senses.example: The novel recounts a dangerous amour in wartime Paris.
senses.exampleCN: 小说讲述了战时巴黎一段危险的恋情。
senses.why: From Latin amor, love: when love must hide, English reaches for the French word.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 amor「爱」：当爱必须隐藏时，英语便借用法语词。

senses.title: A love affair in general, literary register
senses.titleCN: 恋情泛称：文学语域的爱恋
senses.definition: a romantic attachment, without necessarily any secrecy, in elevated style
senses.definitionCN: 书卷语域中的浪漫恋情，不必然隐秘
senses.example: His early amours filled three volumes of letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他早年的恋情感事写满了三卷书信。
senses.why: The word keeps its French elegance, so writers use it for romance as a subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了法语的雅致，作家便用它来谈论作为主题的爱情。

senses.title: Courtly love in chivalric tradition
senses.titleCN: 骑士之爱：典雅爱情传统
senses.definition: the idealized, ritualized love of medieval courtly literature
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪骑士文学中理想化、仪式化的爱情
senses.example: The knight pledged service to his lady in the fashion of courtly amour.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士以典雅爱情的方式向贵妇人宣誓效忠。
senses.why: Medieval romance codified love into duties; the borrowed word carries that ritual air.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪骑士文学把爱情规则化，这个借词因此带有仪式感。

senses.title: The beloved person
senses.definition: a person with whom one has a love affair; a lover
senses.definitionCN: 恋爱关系的对象；爱人
senses.example: He wrote poem after poem to his amour.
senses.exampleCN: 他为恋人写了一首又一首诗。
senses.why: The feeling word slides onto the person who causes it.
senses.whyCN: 指情感的词会滑向引发情感的人。

intro.en: Amour is the French form of Latin amor, love, borrowed into English with a hint of secrecy.
intro.cn: amour 是拉丁语 amor（爱）的法语形式，借入英语后带上一丝隐秘色彩。

items.en: Root *am-, to love.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *am-「爱」。

items.en: amor, love; the root verb is amare.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amor「爱」，动词原形为 amare。

items.en: amour, both the feeling of love and a love affair.
items.cn: 古法语 amour，既指爱之情感，也指一段恋情。

items.en: English borrows amour, at first simply meaning love.
items.cn: 十三世纪中世纪英语借入 amour，最初只表示「爱」。

items.en: The sense narrows to love affairs, often scandalous ones.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪词义收窄为恋情，且常带绯闻色彩。

items.en: Now a literary word for a romantic or secret affair.
items.cn: 如今是表示浪漫或隐秘恋情的文学用语。

note.en: Tell amour apart from its love-root relatives and from rival affair words.
note.cn: 把 amour 与「爱」词根的亲属词区分开，并与其他「风流韵事」用词对比。

entries.definition: adjective showing love; amour is the affair itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「多情的」；amour 是恋情本身，同根易混。

entries.definition: the person in an illicit affair; amour is the relationship, paramour the lover.
entries.definitionCN: 不正当的恋人；amour 指关系，paramour 指人，同根注意分工。

entries.definition: one who loves an activity unpaid; same root am-, different branch.
entries.definitionCN: 业余爱好者；同属 am- 词根但语义分支不同，勿混。

entries.definition: a romantic involvement, often secret; the plain modern word.
entries.definitionCN: 婚外情、恋情；现代最常用的普通说法。

entries.definition: a secret romantic link, French loanword like amour.
entries.definitionCN: 私情；与 amour 同为法语借词。

entries.definition: a secret meeting between lovers.
entries.definitionCN: 幽会；强调情人秘密会面。

normalIntro.en: Hear the love inside amour directly.
normalIntro.cn: 直接听出 amour 里的「爱」。

normal.en: amour is literally French for love.
normal.cn: amour 就是法语「爱」这个词本身。

normal.en: Family: amorous (adj.), amour (affair), paramour (lover).
normal.cn: 词族：amorous（多情的）、amour（恋情）、paramour（情人）。

normal.en: Cinema cue: Amour is an Oscar-winning French film about love.
normal.cn: 电影提示：《爱》是获奥斯卡奖的法国爱情片，片名即 amour。

normal.en: Add par- for paramour: the lover through (par) an amour.
normal.cn: 加 par- 成 paramour：穿过这段恋情的恋人。

normal.en: Register note: amour is literary; affair is everyday.
normal.cn: 语域提示：amour 偏书面，affair 是日常词。

abstract.en: A folded letter passed under a ballroom door — amour in one image.
abstract.cn: 舞厅门缝下递进的折起的信——一个画面就是 amour。

abstract.en: Two masked eyes at a Paris balcony at midnight.
abstract.cn: 午夜巴黎阳台上一双蒙面的眼睛。

abstract.en: Say 'a-MOOR' and picture love anchored secretly in a hidden harbor.
abstract.cn: 读 a-MOOR 时联想「秘密泊进港湾的爱」。

examples.en: The diaries reveal the statesman's lifelong amours.
examples.cn: 日记披露了这位政治家一生中的多段恋情。

examples.en: Scandal erupted when the princess's amour reached the press.
examples.cn: 王妃的恋情见报后，丑闻轰然爆发。

examples.en: Medieval poets celebrated the ideal of courtly amour.
examples.cn: 中世纪诗人歌颂典雅爱情理想。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿姆」——恋人们互相喊对方「阿姆（ma 母音倒装）」，亲昵到只肯低声叫，像藏着一段秘密恋情。

root: 拉丁语 amare（爱）→ amor（爱情）→ 古法语 amour → 十三世纪借入英语。同根词：amorous（多情的）、paramour（情人）、amateur（爱好者）、enamor（使迷恋）。

sensesIntro.en: Amour runs from hidden affairs through literary romance and courtly ritual love to the beloved person.
sensesIntro.cn: amour 从隐秘恋情出发，经文学浪漫与骑士式爱情，延伸到恋人本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: love that must hide its face
core.cn: 核心意象：必须蒙住脸的爱

branches.en: The hidden, improper relationship
branches.cn: 隐秘越界的恋爱关系

branches.en: Literary love as a subject
branches.cn: 作为文学主题的爱情

branches.en: Ritualized medieval courtly love
branches.cn: 仪式化的中世纪典雅爱情

branches.en: The person loved
branches.cn: 被爱的人

branches.en: Romance as elegant literary matter
branches.cn: 作为雅致文学素材的爱情

intro.en: Amour is pure amor dressed in French spelling, joined in English to a family of love words.
intro.cn: amour 就是换了法语拼写的 amor，在英语中汇入「爱」词家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin amor generates English words from passion to hobbies.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 amor 派生出英语中从爱情到爱好的众多词汇。

items.example: amor vincit omnia, love conquers all
items.exampleCN: amor vincit omnia 即「爱战胜一切」
